input:
If you decide to eat here, just be aware it is going to take about 2 hours from beginning to end. We have tried it multiple times, because I want to like it! I have been to it's other locations in NJ and never had a bad experience. 

The food is good, but it takes a very long time to come out. The waitstaff is very young, but usually pleasant. We have just had too many experiences where we spent way too long waiting. We usually opt for another diner or restaurant on the weekends, in order to be done quicker.
Refine this for me please:
If you dine here, expect the experience to take around two hours from start to finish. We’ve returned multiple times because I genuinely want to like it—the food is good, and I’ve never had a bad experience at their other New Jersey locations.

However, the meals consistently take a very long time to arrive. The waitstaff, while young and usually pleasant, cannot offset the prolonged waits we’ve repeatedly endured. For this reason, we now typically choose another diner or restaurant on weekends to ensure a quicker meal.

input:
I've taken a lot of spin classes over the years, and nothing compares to the classes at Body Cycle. From the nice, clean space and amazing bikes, to the welcoming and motivating instructors, every class is a top notch work out.

For anyone who struggles to fit workouts in, the online scheduling system makes it easy to plan ahead (and there's no need to line up way in advanced like many gyms make you do).

There is no way I can write this review without giving Russell, the owner of Body Cycle, a shout out. Russell's passion for fitness and cycling is so evident, as is his desire for all of his clients to succeed. He is always dropping in to classes to check in/provide encouragement, and is open to ideas and recommendations from anyone. Russell always wears a smile on his face, even when he's kicking your butt in class!
Refine this for me please:
After years of taking spin classes, nothing rivals the experience at Body Cycle. The studio is immaculate, the bikes are superb, and the instructors are both welcoming and incredibly motivating, ensuring every session is a top-tier workout.

For busy schedules, their online booking system is a lifesaver, allowing you to plan effortlessly without the hassle of long sign-up queues common at other gyms.

I must give a special commendation to the owner, Russell. His passion for fitness and cycling is palpable, matched by a genuine commitment to every client's success. He frequently visits classes to offer encouragement, is always open to feedback, and radiates a positive energy—even when he’s pushing you to your absolute limit.

input: Family diner. Had the buffet. Eclectic assortment: a large chicken leg, fried jalapeño, tamale, two rolled grape leaves, fresh melon. All good. Lots of Mexican choices there. Also has a menu with breakfast served all day long. Friendly, attentive staff. Good place for a casual relaxed meal with no expectations. Next to the Clarion Hotel.
Refine this for me please: A family diner offering a buffet with an eclectic mix, like chicken, jalapeños, tamales, grape leaves, and melon. Many Mexican options and an all-day breakfast menu. The staff is friendly and attentive, making it ideal for a casual, relaxed meal. It’s located next to the Clarion Hotel.

input: Wow!  Yummy, different,  delicious.   Our favorite is the lamb curry and korma.  With 10 different kinds of naan!!!  Don't let the outside deter you (because we almost changed our minds)...go in and try something new!   You'll be glad you did!
Refine this for me please: The lamb curry and korma are delicious, and with ten kinds of naan, it's a unique treat. Don't be put off by the exterior—venture inside for a meal you won't regret.

input: Cute interior and owner (?) gave us tour of upcoming patio/rooftop area which will be great on beautiful days like today. Cheese curds were very good and very filling. Really like that sandwiches come w salad, esp after eating too many curds! Had the onion, gruyere, tomato sandwich. Wasn't too much cheese which I liked. Needed something else...pepper jelly maybe. Would like to see more menu options added such as salads w fun cheeses. Lots of beer and wine as well as limited cocktails. Next time I will try one of the draft wines.
Refine this for me please:
The cozy interior was charming, and the owner kindly showed us the future patio and rooftop space—perfect for a day like this. The cheese curds were excellent and surprisingly filling. I appreciated that sandwiches include a salad, especially after indulging in the curds. My onion, Gruyère, and tomato sandwich was good, though it needed a lift, perhaps with pepper jelly. I’d love more options, like salads featuring interesting cheeses. The drink selection is strong, with plenty of beer and wine plus some cocktails. Next visit, I’m trying a draft wine.

input: Loved this tour! I grabbed a groupon and the price was great. It was the perfect way to explore New Orleans for someone who'd never been there before and didn't know a lot about the history of the city. Our tour guide had tons of interesting tidbits about the city, and I really enjoyed the experience. Highly recommended tour. I actually thought we were just going to tour through the cemetery, but she took us around the French Quarter for the first hour, and the cemetery for the second half of the tour. You'll meet up in front of a grocery store (seems strange at first, but it's not terribly hard to find, and it'll give you a chance to get some water), and you'll stop at a visitor center part way through the tour for a bathroom break if needed. This tour was one of my favorite parts of my trip!
Refine this for me please:
This tour was a highlight of my trip to New Orleans! As a first-time visitor with little knowledge of the city's history, it was the perfect introduction. I found a great deal through Groupon. Our guide was fantastic, sharing tons of fascinating tidbits throughout the experience.

The tour structure was a welcome surprise: we spent the first hour exploring the French Quarter before dedicating the second half to the cemetery. The meeting point is in front of a grocery store, which seems odd but is easy to locate and allows you to grab water beforehand. A mid-tour stop at a visitor center also provides a convenient bathroom break.

I highly recommend this engaging and well-paced tour—it was absolutely one of my favorite activities.

input: Amazingly amazing wings and homemade bleu cheese. Had the ribeye: tender, perfectly prepared, delicious. Nice selection of craft beers. Would DEFINITELY recommend checking out this hidden gem.

input: This easter instead of going to Lopez Lake we went to Los Padres National Forest which is really pretty but if you go to white rock the staff needs to cut down all the dead grass that invades the rock and the water. I would wish the staff would also clean or get rid of the dead grass that's also living by the water. The water is really green and dirty. Los padres national forest staff need to work hard to maintain this forest looking pretty and not like a dumpster. Even Cachuma lake looks like they put a bit more effort.
Refine this for me please: This Easter, we visited Los Padres National Forest instead of Lopez Lake. The area is beautiful, but at White Rock, the invasive dead grass covering the rock and water edge needs to be cut back. I also wish staff would clear the dead grass accumulating along the shoreline. The water itself is unpleasantly green and murky. The forest service must work harder to maintain the area's natural beauty; currently, it feels neglected. By comparison, even nearby Cachuma Lake appears better maintained.

input: Had a party of 6 here for hibachi. Our waitress brought our separate sushi orders on one plate so we couldn't really tell who's was who's and forgot several items on an order. Usually hibachi is a fun lively experience and our  cook  said maybe three words, but he cooked very well his name was Francisco. Refine this for me please: Our party of six came for hibachi. The waitress combined our separate sushi orders onto a single plate, making it impossible to distinguish them, and she also forgot several items. Mistakes happen, but the restaurant was very quiet, so the errors were surprising. Typically, hibachi is a lively experience, yet our cook, Francisco, was nearly silent—though his cooking was excellent. The service felt off, while the food was pretty good. I hope it was just an unusual night, but for the price, I wouldn’t return.

input:
My experience with Shalimar was nothing but wonderful. 
I wanted to get my engagement ring sized and was told over the phone that it could probably be done within the day. 
When I brought it by, the team confirmed that the jeweler would be able to accommodate my same-day request and that it would be around $40 (simple band, decrease by three full sizes).
I checked my size one more time, confirmed, and left to let them do their thing.
When I came to pick up later that afternoon, the ring was too small. It's very important to note that Shalimar sized the ring perfectly, but that I made a mistake and should've gone up a half-size.
The Shalimar group were completely understanding and accommodating, even resizing my ring back up and getting it back to me within an hour at no charge! Even though it was my mistake!
The associates' attitudes in dealing with what was a pretty embarrassing situation instantly earned my satisfaction and loyalty as a customer. Very grateful for such a wonderful experience.
Refine this for me please:
My experience with Shalimar was exceptional. I needed my engagement ring resized and was informed by phone it could likely be done the same day. Upon arrival, the team confirmed the jeweler could accommodate my request, estimating a cost of around $40 for resizing the simple band down three sizes. I double-checked my size, confirmed it, and left the ring with them.

When I returned that afternoon, the ring was too tight. Crucially, Shalimar had sized it perfectly to my initial instruction; the error was mine, as I needed a half-size larger. Despite this being my mistake, the team was utterly understanding and accommodating. They promptly resized the ring upward and had it ready for me within an hour—at no additional charge.

The associates’ compassionate and professional handling of an embarrassing situation instantly secured my satisfaction and loyalty. I am deeply grateful for such a wonderful and patient customer service experience.

input: Locals recommended Milktooth, and it's an amazing jewel of Indianapolis. I'm glade I had the chance to experience this.

input:
The bun makes the Sonoran Dog. It's like a snuggie for the pup. A first, it seems ridiculous and almost like it's going to be too much, exactly like everyone's favorite blanket with sleeves. Too much softness, too much smush, too indulgent.  Wrong. It's warm, soft, chewy, fragrant, and it succeeds where other famed Sonoran Dogs fail. 

The hot dog itself is flavorful, but I would prefer that it or the bacon have a little more bite or snap to better hold their own against the dominant mustard and onions. 

I'm with the masses on the carne asada caramelo. Excellent tortilla, salty, melty cheese, and great carne. 

Super cheap and you can drive through.
Refine this for me please:
The bun is essential to the Sonoran Dog, acting like a snug blanket for the frankfurter. At first, its soft, indulgent abundance seems excessive, but it proves to be warm, fragrant, and perfectly chewy—succeeding where others fail.

While the hot dog is flavorful, I wish it or the bacon had more snap to stand up to the bold mustard and onions.

I agree with popular opinion on the carne asada caramelo: an excellent tortilla with salty, melted cheese and superb meat.

It’s all very affordable, and the drive-through option makes it even better.

input: Great place for breakfast! I had the waffle, which was fluffy and perfect, and home fries which were nice and smashed and crunchy. Friendly waitstaff. Will definitely be back!

input: Upland is a brewery based out of Bloomington, Indiana that has become popular enough to open up a couple additional locations in central Indiana.  All of their beers are very good, and I am also a fan of their burgers and tenderloins.  Therefore, I was excited to try their pizza, but I don't think it ended up being on par with these other items.  My margherita pizza had a cracker-like crust and was pretty light overall.  The cheese was good, but none of the other toppings added much flavor.  There was no red sauce as is typical for a true margherita pizza.  My opinion is that Upland's pizza might serve as a nice appetizer for a group, but I'll be sticking with their burgers or tenderloins as my meal of choice on future visits.
Refine this for me please:
Upland, a popular brewery from Bloomington, Indiana, has expanded with several locations across the state. While I consistently enjoy their excellent beers, burgers, and tenderloins, their pizza fell short of my expectations. The margherita pizza I ordered featured a very thin, cracker-like crust and was overall quite light. Although the cheese was good, the other toppings lacked distinctive flavor, and it notably omitted the red sauce characteristic of a true margherita. In my view, Upland’s pizza could work well as a shareable appetizer for a table. However, on future visits, I will continue to choose their superb burgers or tenderloins as my primary meal.

input:
I was really between 3 and 4 stars for this one. I LOVE the 96th street Naked Tchopstix so I was very excited to see this one which is closer to my house.
The vibe is totally different as this is geared more to take out although they do have a decent size dining area. You order at the counter and they deliver it.
My daughter and I tried the sushi bowl. You pick up a piece of paper and  select from a choice of proteins, vegetables, rice and toppings. I like the fact that it is on paper and you don't have to guess what things are or have to shout over the counter to tell the server what you want. The sushi bowl was good but not wonderful. The choices particularly of the vegetables seemed a little too limiting and I felt I had more rice than other food items. The sauces were tasty. My husband ordered the Maui roll which is my favorite roll at the 96th street location and this just was not up that standard. It was good but the quality and consistently was not as good as at 96th street. I would go back though and I think a lot of people would be happy with the sushi bowls. I do want to make a comment about the low reviews that people have given the place because of service. People - it is a sushi place - it isn't McDonalds- so it will be a bit slower. You are not going to order and get out of there in five minutes even though it is called express. As a healthy alternative to fast food in the area, it is worth the wait. Oh and try the bubble tea. I had the strawberry and it was quite yummy. Next time I am going to try the vanilla chai.
Refine this for me please:
I was torn between three and four stars for this location. As a fan of the 96th Street Naked Tchopstix, I was excited to find a branch closer to home.

The vibe here is completely different, geared more toward takeout, though they do have a reasonably sized dining area. Service is counter-order, with delivery to your table.

My daughter and I tried the build-your-own sushi bowl. You mark your selections on a paper checklist, choosing from proteins, vegetables, rice, and toppings. I appreciated this system—it’s clear and eliminates the need to shout your order across the counter. The bowl was good, but not exceptional. The vegetable choices felt somewhat limited, and my portion seemed overly heavy on rice. The sauces, however, were quite tasty. My husband ordered the Maui roll, a favorite of mine at the 96th Street location, and it didn’t quite meet that standard. It was still good, but the quality and consistency weren’t the same.

I would return, and I believe many would be satisfied with the sushi bowls as a healthy, fast-casual option. I also want to address the low reviews citing slow service. This is a sushi restaurant, not fast food—even with “Express” in the name, don’t expect to be in and out in five minutes. As a fresher alternative to typical fast food in the area, it’s worth a short wait.

Finally, don’t skip the bubble tea. The strawberry flavor was delicious, and I look forward to trying the vanilla chai next time.

input: We checked in around 2:30 pm.  Check-in was quick and easy with complimentary valet parking (always appreciated).  The Peppermill is huge and reminded us of the Caesars Palace in Las Vegas.  They have around eight restaurants on site offering almost any type of food you could want.  The casino area is huge, rivaling almost anything you could find in Las Vegas.  One thing we noticed is that many of the slot machines were noted as being penny machines, but when you actually started to play them you realized they had minimum bets of anywhere from 30 cents to $5.  Talk about false advertising!  We were in the Tuscany Tower on the 12th floor.  Our room had a nice view of the huge pool area.  Our room was large and featured free WiFi (likewise always appreciated), a huge bathroom area with large shower (with two shower heads), TV, a large jetted bathtub and a phone next to the commode.  There were dual sinks and lots of counter space.  Plenty of towels were supplied.  The roomy main area had a king bed with night stands, closet, TV, mini fridge, dresser with two drawers, a safe, table for computer or writing, complimentary bottles of water, and three nicely upholstered chairs and table.  The thermostat did a good job controlling the temperature and keeping it comfortable.  Staff were all courteous and helpful.  A very nice place and we enjoyed our stay.
Refine this for me please:
We arrived at 2:30 pm for a swift and easy check-in, which included complimentary valet parking—a welcome perk. The Peppermill’s vast scale immediately brought Caesars Palace in Las Vegas to mind. The resort boasts around eight on-site restaurants, covering nearly every cuisine imaginable, and its casino floor is enormous, rivaling those found on the Strip.

A notable observation was the slot machines: many were labeled as penny slots, yet the minimum bets actually ranged from 30 cents to $5—a clear case of false advertising.

Our room was located on the 12th floor of the Tuscany Tower, offering a pleasant view of the expansive pool area. It was spacious and well-appointed, featuring free WiFi, a large bathroom with dual sinks, a two-headed shower, a jetted tub, and even a phone beside the commode. Ample towels and counter space were provided.

The main room contained a king bed with nightstands, a closet, a TV, a mini fridge, a dresser, a safe, a work table, complimentary water, and three upholstered chairs with a table. The thermostat maintained a consistently comfortable temperature.

Throughout our stay, all staff members were courteous and helpful. It was a very nice experience, and we thoroughly enjoyed our visit.

The good: price, location, dessert (edible food items are: baked chicken, fried chicken, mashed potatoes, Salad bar lol, meat and cheese bar, ravioli, pizza) also our waitress was bomb af

The meh: behind counter meat slicing station, shrimp (not even deveined), Mexican station

The bad: breakfast -worst eggs ever, actually worst, eggs. Le Benedict can't even cut through ham or English muffin (tried on all 3 occasions), steak, shrimp again, hell breaded items can't even, don't even. Decor it's the 1970 nightmare you can imagine

Tried 3 times and failed
Refine this for me please:
This buffet is affordable and conveniently located, but the quality is consistently low. While the price, location, and desserts are positives, and our waitress was excellent, the food is largely disappointing. The baked chicken, fried chicken, and salad bar are edible, but many stations—like the meat slicer, Mexican fare, and shrimp (which isn't even deveined)—are mediocre.

The breakfast is particularly bad, featuring terrible eggs and a failed Eggs Benedict with uncuttable ham and muffins. The steak and breaded items are inedible, and the decor is a dated 1970s nightmare. Despite three attempts, the experience never improved.

**(Word count: 101)**

input:
The only reason I didn't give this restaurant a 5 star rating, is because of one single pretentious waiter. As a 4 night guest at Hotel Palomar, the location of the restaurant is an obvious plus. The first night of my stay, I met a coworker in the restaurant for a cocktail. When we arrived, the host staff were busy and not available, so we just walked in. The restaurant was not too busy, so we just looked at a small table next to the bar and proceeded to take a seat. A waiter came by and I quickly asked if we could have a seat, before sitting down and told him we'd only be having cocktails. He stumbled on his reply, and in an irritated/in-convinced tone, told me "I guess it would be fine" and basically just kept walking mid sentence. My guest and I brushed it off, and started having a conversation while looking at the drink menu. To make a long story short, he was distant and we both got the "couldn't be bothered" vibe from him. When it came to the bill, we asked if it could be split due to company transaction policies, and you would have thought asked him for some inconceivable task. We basically spent the rest of our night and elevator ride to our room in shock of the rudeness we had just experienced. 

Although that situation left a bad taste in our mouth, and the night before we decided to avoid the restaurant, we decided to grab another cocktail and give this place one more try. After looking around and ensuring "last nights waiter" wasn't on shift, we walked over to the bar and started looking over the menu. Instantly, the bartender greeted us with pleasant small talk and made us feel 100% welcome. He asked about our day, recommended cocktails and was a completely genuine person. This guy (I think his name was Ben) is an absolute star! He gave us lessons on Whiskey, described how to make classic cocktails, and was 100% invested in our experience. This is exactly what a bartender at a 4/5 star establishment should be - actually he exceeds that. He was kind, funny, friendly and completely redeemed this restaurant/bar from our terrible experience the night before. 
I also ordered room service last night from this restaurant, and it was amazing. The bacon wrapped dates and chocolate cake are to die for! Great restaurant and amazing bartender(s). Too bad one bad egg could have spoiled this experience.
Refine this for me please:
My decision to withhold a fifth star from this otherwise excellent restaurant hinges entirely on a single, pretentious waiter. As a guest at the Hotel Palomar for four nights, the restaurant’s convenient location was a major perk. On my first evening, I met a colleague there for a cocktail. Finding the host stand unattended, we entered the mostly empty space and selected a small table near the bar. Before sitting, I proactively caught a passing waiter to ask if it was acceptable, explaining we only wanted drinks. His response was dismissive; with an irritated and unconvinced tone, he muttered, “I guess it would be fine,” and walked away mid-sentence.

We brushed it off, but his “couldn’t be bothered” attitude persisted throughout our visit. The pinnacle of his rudeness came when we requested separate checks for company expense purposes. He reacted as if we’d asked for something utterly inconceivable. The interaction was so jarring that my colleague and I spent the rest of the evening, including our elevator ride upstairs, in stunned disbelief.

That experience left such a bad taste that we avoided the restaurant the following night. However, on our third night, we decided to give it another chance, first confirming that the problematic waiter was not on duty. We approached the bar and were instantly greeted by a bartender—I believe his name was Ben. The contrast was night and day. With genuine warmth, he engaged us in pleasant small talk, asked about our day, and offered excellent cocktail recommendations. He was an absolute star, giving us impromptu lessons on whiskey and the art of classic cocktails, fully invested in crafting a wonderful experience. Ben embodies—and even exceeds—the standard for a bartender at a fine establishment: kind, funny, friendly, and utterly professional. He single-handedly redeemed the restaurant from our prior poor impression.

I should also note that the room service I ordered from the restaurant last night was exceptional; the bacon-wrapped dates and chocolate cake are to die for. This is, overall, a great restaurant with an amazing bar team. It’s a testament to their quality that one bad egg nearly spoiled the entire experience, yet the excellence of staff like Ben ultimately shines through.

input: Stopped by after a Sunday morning walk in the park - great food, coffee customer service - love the vibe in here
Refine this for me please:
Stopped in after a Sunday park walk. The food, coffee, and service were great, and I love the vibe here.

(22 words)

input: In a word... "OVERRATED!".  The food took forever to come out.  The burger was WAY overcooked (Especially when I ordered it Medium Rare) and the Seafood Jumbalaya was Decent.  Not worth the price.  There are better places to eat in the french quarter.  It was not horrible, but for everything that we had heard about this place, I would have expected much better.
Refine this for me please: In a single word: overrated. The service was slow, and my burger arrived well-done instead of medium-rare. The seafood jambalaya was merely decent. Given the price and its reputation in the French Quarter, I expected far better. While not terrible, there are superior dining options nearby.

input: Comfortable bed, good breakfast, fast internet, great location, and low price. Overall I was really impressed with this place. However, if you stay on the top floors you may be waiting up to 15 minutes for an elevator in the morning.
Refine this for me please: This place impressed me with its comfortable bed, good breakfast, fast internet, great location, and low price. However, morning elevator waits for top-floor guests can be up to 15 minutes.

input: NEVER AGAIN. This is a so called restaurant that does nothing that a restaurant should other than prepare food, because the rest is done by the patron. Want water? Get up and go across the yard to get it. Want a drink, walk up a flight of stairs and pay cash. Want to sit in a dirty yard in dirty lawn chairs, enjoy yourself. The wait staff is mildy helpful in that they bring you your food after you go to the window and pay cash for it...kind of like New Orleans Hamburger and Seafood, but dirty and with live music (which is nice). It's a one in a lifetime experience for me...just once.
Refine this for me please:
NEVER AGAIN. This establishment performs only the bare minimum function of a restaurant: preparing food. Everything else is left to the patron. You fetch your own water from across the yard. You climb a flight of stairs to pay cash for a drink. You sit in a grimy courtyard on dirty lawn chairs. The staff is marginally helpful, delivering your food only after you pay cash at the window—reminiscent of a fast-food joint, but dirtier. The live music was pleasant, but it cannot redeem the experience. For me, this was a one-in-a-lifetime visit. Once was enough.

(Word count: 104)

input:
If you want to pay for everything a la carte this is the place for you.  
Food wasn't terrible not impressive.
They brought a basket of chips and some tomato sauce which I asked politely for something spicier and some pico de gallo.  She brought them happily to me and the salsa was much better.  When asked what we would like to drink I asked for a coke and she brought out a bottle which I stated I wanted the fountain drink.  She said "oh that's only Pepsi".  Never mentioned that they only had bottle drinks for coke.  
We ordered our food which was reasonably priced, asked for sour cream and also to put cheese on the taco.  She let us know cheese was extra.  
It was $2.50 extra for another basket of chips.  
When I received the bill we paid more for the condiments then the actual food.  Side of sour cream 2.00, pico de gallo 2.50, salsa 2.00, chips 2.50, cheese 1.00 and the bottled coke that we didn't want 5.00.  
Just a suggestion...when you order anything make sure to ask if there is an extra charge.
Refine this for me please:
If you prefer to pay à la carte for every item, this restaurant will suit you. The food wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t impressive either.

We were brought a basket of chips with tomato sauce. I politely asked for something spicier and some pico de gallo, which the server happily provided—the salsa was much better. When ordering drinks, I asked for a Coke and was brought a bottle. I explained I wanted a fountain drink, to which she replied, “Oh, that’s only Pepsi.” She never mentioned bottled drinks were the only option for Coke.

We ordered reasonably priced food and requested sour cream and cheese on a taco. We were informed cheese was extra. Another basket of chips cost $2.50.

Upon receiving the bill, I realized we paid more for condiments than the actual meal: sour cream $2.00, pico de gallo $2.50, salsa $2.00, chips $2.50, cheese $1.00, and the unwanted bottled Coke for $5.00.

My suggestion: always ask if there’s an extra charge when ordering anything here.

Word count: 173

input: The cafe was extremely cute. We came at 8am and they even had a jazz band playing at that time. I got the breakfast sandwich and it was delicious. I loved how they rolled the egg and put the bacon pieces inside. Great price for a filling breakfast!
Refine this for me please: This charming cafe surprised us with a live jazz band at 8 a.m. I ordered their delicious breakfast sandwich, where the egg is rolled around pieces of bacon. It was a very filling meal for a great price.

input:
On a scale of one to things that are awesome, this place is the bomb. 

I was drawn in by the promise of the duckfat frenchfries. Took the boy for his birthday and put our name in, had a drink around the corner while we waited and were given seats at the bar after about 45 minutes. 

We were waited on by Keith, the bartender, who was congenial, knowledgeable about his whiskeys and an all-around cool guy. We started with 3 cape may salts (two for me, one for the boy) and tater tots, both of which made me happy.

For dinner, I got Kentucky Fried Quail (stellar, though the succotash was not as exciting as I wanted it to be) and the boy got the 24$ Fois Gras burger, which was incredible. Worth every penny. The duckfat fries were pretty yummy, but not even the best part of the meal. I could've done without the cheese sauce, but as it was on the side I wasn't deterred.

I look forward to coming back here, with everyone I know.
Refine this for me please:
On a scale of one to awesome, this place is phenomenal.

My son and I visited for his birthday, lured by the famous duckfat fries. After putting our name down, we enjoyed a drink nearby during the 45-minute wait before being seated at the bar.

Our bartender, Keith, was congenial, whiskey-knowledgeable, and an all-around cool guy. We began with three Cape May Salts and tater tots—a perfect start.

For dinner, I had the stellar Kentucky Fried Quail (though its succotash was underwhelming). My son ordered the $24 foie gras burger, which was incredible and worth every penny. The duckfat fries were delicious, yet not the meal’s highlight. The optional cheese sauce was unnecessary, but easily skipped.

I can’t wait to return and bring everyone I know.

(Word count: 179)

input: We started with the artichoke dip, big mistake. It was cold and the chips were stale. Mentioned to our waitress, but nothing came of it. input: It was my fiance's birthday and he decided he wanted a good, laid back Thai restaurant for dinner. Yelp steered us in the Jasmine Rice direction, and it was definitely a good decision. We wanted the summer rolls, which were on the menu, but apparently will not be available until summer, so we settled on the pan-fried dumplings. The flavor was good, but I don't think we'd order them again. We got the green curry fried rice with duck and chicken pad thai. Both of those dishes were great, but the duck stole the show. That was some the of tastiest duck I've ever had. The pad thai was a bit sweet for us, so I think we'd try a different noodle dish when we return. But it was still very good, especially with some chili sauce mixed in. Our service was good, but other people had issues. One table was rushing to get to a show at the Kimmel Center and waited quite a while for their meal (and were going to be late). Another person who got take-out was missing one of their items (but the owner realized it and called him and walked the dish to his house, which was very nice). Overall, good quality Thai! We would definitely go back.
Refine this for me please:
For my fiancé’s birthday, he wanted a relaxed Thai dinner. Yelp recommended Jasmine Rice, which proved to be an excellent choice. We initially sought the summer rolls, but learned they’re seasonal, so we opted for pan-fried dumplings instead. They were flavorful, though not something we’d reorder.

Our main courses were the green curry fried rice with duck and the chicken pad thai. Both were delicious, but the duck was exceptional—among the best I’ve ever tasted. The pad thai leaned sweet for our preference, so next time we’ll try a different noodle dish. That said, it was still very good, especially with a dash of chili sauce.

Service was attentive for us, though we noticed hiccups elsewhere. One couple, hurrying to a show at the Kimmel Center, endured a long wait for their meal. Another customer’s take-out order was missing an item, but the owner personally called and delivered it to their home—a very kind gesture.

Overall, Jasmine Rice offers great quality Thai food. We will definitely return.

You know you have a great stylist when you don't have to specify what you want done, but instead they see what needs to be done. Great stylist, great personality and very knowledgeable. Refine this for me please:
Courtney is simply the best hairstylist I’ve ever had. What makes her exceptional is her keen eye for what truly suits me, and over the past year she has expertly learned my style boundaries. I now walk in and simply tell her to do what she thinks is best—and I’m always blown away by the result. input:

Refine this for me please:
The Brewpub is a favorite for its variety, offering everything from nachos and pizza to sandwiches, plus a great selection of house-crafted beers. Be prepared for a leisurely pace, however, as service is consistently slow. This isn't a quick bite, but a place to savor time with friends on the patio. It’s wonderfully inclusive, welcoming kids, dogs, vegetarians, and vegans. My personal go-tos are the half-order nachos or the fish & chips. Their seasonal Pumpkin Beer is also excellent, rivaling my top favorites.

(Word count: 101)

input:
My go to menu is coconut soup and pad thai with protein. I tried same menu here. 
Actually really like their coconut soup. They used enough amount of coconut milk that soup was really creamy and wasn't over powering with herb. I am so used to Americanized thai cuisine that I prefer less herb on my dish except cilantro.
Pat thai was great too. Liked the amount of peanut they used, noodle was chewy and perfect and not too sweet. They gave me generous amount of chicken and white meat wasn't dry so I was very happy with my meal.
Refine this for me please:
My usual order is coconut soup and pad thai with chicken. I tried both here and was very pleased. Their coconut soup is excellent—creamy from ample coconut milk, but not overpowered by herbs. As someone accustomed to Americanized Thai food, I prefer subtler herb flavors (cilantro aside).

The pad thai was also great: a perfect chewy texture, balanced sweetness, and a generous amount of peanuts. They provided plenty of chicken, and the white meat was moist and tender. It was a satisfying meal overall.

input: Excellent service! Great diner food and breakfast is served all day. Came here for lunch- they were busy but very friendly and hospitable. Easy to get to off the 295.

input:
We were a bit weary about trying the Shellfish Company on the Wharf as more often than not, many places like these (see Cannery Row, Monterey) feast on a captive audience and provide sub-standard fare at high prices.

However, emboldened by the perennial good reviews on Yelp, we suppressed our initial observations and went ahead with the trying it out. The place is small, so definitely plan ahead. You will have to wait, so either you know, just do so, or perhaps try to visit outside of peak hours. Luckily, our wait was only about 20 minutes as the dinner rush was just leveling off.

The special was the local rock crab - $25 for 3 lbs of California Rock Crab, salad, and your choice of soup/chowder. After taking a look at a few trays of rock crab being served out, the wife and I both opted for it, as it looked awesome.  

The salad/chowder combo was great as you actually received hearty portions of each, so it was a good start. As much as I liked the chowder however, the Shrimp Bisque the wife ordered was amazing, so I would recommend that going forward. 

But enough of prattling on about side dishes: the rock crab tasted just as glorious as it looked. Juicy, buttery chunks of white crab meat await you, just a few cracks away. While the rock crab shells are pretty thick, once cracked, they splinter and separate easily, a good sign they are cooked to perfection. The rock crabs provided a great amount of meat for what I felt to be the least amount of work you're going to do for crab, King or otherwise. 

We were thoroughly satisfied with our meal and along with the special being an overall great value, devouring the Rock Crab at SBSC turned out to be one of the favorite meals on the trip. I think ordering crab here is a safe proposition indeed.
Refine this for me please:
We were initially wary of trying the Shellfish Company on the Wharf, as venues in such tourist-centric locations—think Cannery Row in Monterey—often serve mediocre food at inflated prices to a captive audience.

Nevertheless, encouraged by consistently strong Yelp reviews, we set aside our skepticism and decided to give it a try. The restaurant is quite small, so planning ahead is essential. Be prepared to wait; either embrace that reality or aim for off-peak hours. Fortunately, our wait was only about twenty minutes, as the dinner rush was beginning to subside.

That evening’s special was local rock crab: $25 for three pounds of California Rock Crab, a salad, and a choice of soup or chowder. After seeing several impressive-looking trays delivered to other tables, my wife and I both chose it.

The meal began well with the salad and chowder—both portions were substantial and satisfying. While the chowder was quite good, my wife’s shrimp bisque was exceptional, and I’d highly recommend it.

But let’s move past the sides: the rock crab was every bit as glorious as it appeared. Inside each cracked shell were juicy, buttery chunks of white meat. Though the shells are thick, they splintered cleanly with little effort—a sure sign of perfect preparation. These crabs yielded a remarkable amount of meat for what felt like the least messy, least labor-intensive crab experience, whether compared to Dungeness, King, or any other variety.

We left thoroughly satisfied. Between the exceptional quality and the outstanding value of the special, our rock crab feast at SBSC ranked among the favorite meals of our entire trip. Ordering crab here isn’t just a good choice—it’s a reliably excellent one.

input: I LOVE Weaver's Way and really disagree with some of the content in previous reviews. WW is not necessarily meant for convenience shopping. I am a single woman and I find that I have no trouble shopping at the co-op, during peak times or otherwise. I actually find the co-op to be a great place to shop if you live alone because I can get smaller quantities of items than if I shop at the corporate stores like Acme. I also enjoy the work hours - I've worked throughout the store, but most recently, I have been getting in my hours by participating in the membership committee. I wouldn't say that the community is necessarily made up of "tree huggers" and "earth children", though. The community is made up of a variety of similarly-minded folks from different backgrounds. I enjoy having a place to go to where I can obtain locally grown produce, a place that offers more natural, wholesome, and preservative-free foods than chain stores with prices way below that of Whole Foods. I enjoy interacting with other members and contributing to my local and global community. I don't find the membership fee or the work hours to be prohibitive being a single person vs. a family. I don't think that membership in a co-op is for everyone and, if you aren't single, it's definitely not a solo decision. If you're keen on being committed to the Weaver Way values, you couldn't find a better place to shop. If not, stick to the chain stores or just pay the 10% visitors' fee to pop in once in a while.
Refine this for me please:
I am a devoted member of Weaver’s Way and feel compelled to offer a different perspective from some previous reviews. The co-op is not designed for convenience shopping in the traditional sense, and that is part of its value. As a single person, I find it perfectly manageable, even during busy times. In fact, it’s ideal for living alone, as I can purchase smaller, more reasonable quantities than at corporate chains like Acme, reducing waste.

I also appreciate the member work requirement. I’ve fulfilled my hours in various roles, most recently on the membership committee, which has been a rewarding way to engage. While some may stereotype the community, it is not exclusively “tree huggers” or “earth children.” Instead, it’s a diverse group of like-minded individuals from all backgrounds, united by shared values.

For me, the benefits are clear: access to locally grown produce, a wide selection of natural and preservative-free foods, and prices significantly lower than Whole Foods. I enjoy interacting with fellow members and knowing my patronage supports both local and global communities. The membership fee and work commitment are not prohibitive, even for a single person versus a family.

That said, a co-op isn’t for everyone. If you have a household, joining is a shared decision. But if you are committed to Weaver’s Way’s principles of community and sustainability, there is no better place to shop. If not, the chain stores are always an option, or you can simply visit the co-op occasionally and pay the 10% non-member surcharge.

input: Traveling through in our RV, stopped over in Granite City. Found this little gem of a cafe. Upon entering, the staff was very sweet and friendly. This is like home cooking. We ate here twice and all our food choices were fresh, delicious and like we would fix at home. Yum.

input: Our family returned for breakfast again this weekend and the food and service was again impeccable ... Highly recommend

input: The kayaking tour at the Santa Cruz Island was great.  My husband and I had a wonderful time.  Jen, our tour guide, was helpful and informative.  We had a lot of fun exploring the caves.  We didn't expect much but this tour definitely exceeded our expectation.

input: Definitely recommend for anyone looking for a delicious meal at a reasonable price. The shrimp and goat cheese crepes are a must have!
Refine this for me please: I highly recommend this spot for a delicious, affordable meal. Their shrimp and goat cheese crepes are essential.

input:
After living in the STL area for way over 10 years now, I am both ashamed and remorseful to admit that I ate here for the FIRST time just a few weeks ago. I am ashamed because it's a St. Louis tradition and remorseful because I missed out on it for so..many...years! 

This place is amazing. What is not to love! It's a factory where you can get a tour (Friday-Sunday, noon-5pm on the hour), there's a shop, bar, and dining area. They also host many event with live music on the weekends. It's fun to just kind of wander and look around - don't worry, you'll get a chance because there will likely be a wait before you dine. The beer is, of course, amazing. The Hefeweizen is my personal favorite and a great start for anyone who is not a huge beer drinker (like myself). Additionally, the food is homegrown and damn good. I had the pizza (recommendation from my server) and it was really spectacular, though I'm admittedly a pizza connoisseur so I enjoy a good pizza pie more than most probably ;P My date had a bison burger which was also really good. 

More fun info: the service is great! I think they tend to hire more funky and alternative people (like tattoo parlor staff) which I support. The quality is what makes this place stand out along with the emphasis on local food and brewery. 

It is a little on the pricier side but for all the experience you get and the quality, it is worth it. I will go again and again and you probably should, too!
Refine this for me please:
Having been a resident of the St. Louis area for well over a decade, I am both ashamed and remorseful to admit that I dined here for the very first time only a few weeks ago. My shame stems from neglecting a local tradition, and my remorse from the many years of excellent experience I missed.

This place is truly amazing. It operates as a functioning factory, offering tours on Fridays through Sundays. Beyond that, it features a shop, a bar, and a dining area, frequently hosting events with live music on weekends. The space invites exploration, and you’ll likely have time to wander, as there’s often a wait for a table. The beer is, of course, superb. My personal favorite is the Hefeweizen—an accessible and excellent choice for those who aren’t avid beer drinkers. The food is homegrown and absolutely delicious. Upon my server’s recommendation, I tried the pizza, which was spectacular (though I confess to being a pizza connoisseur). My date had a bison burger that was also remarkably good.

Further elevating the experience is the outstanding service. The staff often has a funky, alternative vibe, which I fully support. The commitment to quality, combined with a strong emphasis on local sourcing and brewing, is what makes this establishment stand out.

While it is somewhat pricier, the overall experience and superior quality make it entirely worth the cost. I plan to return again and again, and I highly recommend you do the same.

input:
If I could give it a zero, I would. I order a plain hamburger, and realized they put  bacon in it (which I am allergic to and unable to eat) after two bites. When I went back to the drive-through window to complain (didn't realize the actual restaurant was open--it was almost 2 after all...), the guy took back the burger, said nothing, and disappeared. And still did not get an apology.

I refuse to go back there after that ordeal, which is a shame, because it's nice to have a variety of places to go to after DT. Guess Freebirds it is!
Refine this for me please:
My experience was so poor I’d give it zero stars. I ordered a plain hamburger but discovered bacon in it after two bites—a serious issue due to my allergy. I returned to the drive-through (the lobby appeared closed near 2 AM), and the employee silently took the burger and left. This ordeal has made me refuse to return, which is disappointing since it’s good to have variety after downtown. Freebirds will have to be my choice from now on.

input: Been here so many times before and all I can say is the food is really good. A hidden gem in Florissant, it has the best Panang curry around. Haven't been to their sister restaurant yet, but I can't seem to want to move on when I am always so satisfied with their fare here.

input: My food only merited maybe two stars but I will give an extra star because I like the menu (and will try more of it) and their design and concept. It was citrusy, for sure, and I love lemon in a tuna melt but perhaps this was lemon zest or something just way too overpowering?  I think next time I will focus on the dishes with cured Italian meats, mortadella and prosciutto.  And also the baked goods, those sounded pretty good, especially the Nutella bruschetta!
Refine this for me please:
While my meal only merited two stars, I’m granting an extra for the appealing menu and overall design. I plan to return and explore more. Unfortunately, the tomato-basil soup resembled a weak marinara, and my tuna melt had a sharp, off-putting flavor. It was citrusy—I enjoy lemon in tuna, but this tasted of overpowering lemon zest. Next visit, I’ll focus on the cured Italian meats like mortadella and prosciutto, along with the baked goods. The Nutella bruschetta, in particular, sounded excellent.

input:
A couple friends and I stopped by for some late night milkshakes and found ourselves at More Than Just Ice Cream. Well, we just got ice cream...not fully taking advantage of what the name implies, but maybe next time.

3 milkshakes: 1 coffee, 1 chocolate, and 1 black&white malt. 

All were pretty good. Definitely satisfied the ice cream craving. I thought my coffee milkshake could have been thicker, same goes for the chocolate. The black&white was plenty thick and was probably the best of the three. Unfortunately, I did not order that one so I settled for my not so creamy coffee.

I did sample some ice cream flavors before setting on a milkshake. I tried the pumpkin pie which was AMAZING. I don't know why I didn't just get this. Maybe a milkshake isn't the way to go here.
Refine this for me please:
My friends and I stopped at More Than Just Ice Cream for a late-night treat, though we only tried the milkshakes this time.

We ordered three: coffee, chocolate, and a black & white malt. They all satisfied our craving, but my coffee shake and the chocolate one could have been thicker. The black & white malt was the clear winner—perfectly thick and delicious. Sadly, that wasn't my order.

Before deciding, I sampled the pumpkin pie ice cream, which was amazing. In hindsight, I should have just gotten a scoop of that. Maybe milkshakes aren't the best choice here after all. Next time, I’ll explore the “more than” part of the menu.

input:

input:

input:
I visited this restaurant 4 times during my 5 days stay. Crazy, right? Here are a list of reasons/pros:

- We were staying a nearby hotel.
- The restaurant opens 11 - 10:30 pretty much every day including new year's day so it fits into our schedule.
- If you are a party of two, chances are you get seated right away.
- $9 per dozen of oysters which is a really great deal by any standard!
- They have a seafood shop next door that sells boiled and fresh seafood to- go.
- Our server (same) is very friendly and recognized us every single time.

Now I want to talk about the reasons why I only give it 3 stars.

- We tried a bunch of stuff which are all pretty mediocre. Raw oysters are not cleaned well. So if your schedule is flexible, go to Superior Seafood during their happy hours for their 50 cents/oyster - better quality and cheaper. Turtle soup has a strange taste so I definitely prefer Felix's. A portion of my boiled shrimps are always mushy somhow, maybe boiled for too long?...
- The ambient is inviting but not comfortable so we basically just finished our food and go. 
- Clean the bathroom!!

Will probably visit again if we stay in the area next time or simply just pick up some seafood quickly.
Refine this for me please:
During my recent five-day trip, I ate at this restaurant four times—which tells you something. Several practical reasons made it our repeated choice: its proximity to our hotel, reliable hours (open 11 a.m.–10:30 p.m., even on New Year’s Day), and minimal wait for two. At $9 per dozen, the oysters are an outstanding deal. The attached seafood shop offers convenient boiled and fresh seafood to-go, and our server was consistently friendly, recognizing us each visit.

Yet, I’ve settled on a three-star rating because several experiences fell short. Many dishes were mediocre: raw oysters were often poorly cleaned (for better quality and price, Superior Seafood’s happy-hour 50-cent oysters are preferable); the turtle soup had an odd flavor compared to Felix’s; and portions of boiled shrimp were frequently mushy, likely overcooked. While the atmosphere is inviting, it isn’t comfortable enough to linger—we ate and left. Also, the bathrooms urgently need attention.

I’d return if I’m nearby again, mainly for the convenience and quick seafood pickup, but not for a standout meal.

input: Skip this train wreck if you are looking for dinner.  Our server was clueless...like we seriously thought she was lost in the restaurant.  Had to ask for setups, water refills, etc.  Ordered chicken parmesan and got eggplant parmesan instead with a fish bone in it.  The drinks were good.
Refine this for me please: Avoid this restaurant for dinner. Our server seemed lost, forcing us to repeatedly ask for basics. The order was wrong—chicken parmesan arrived as eggplant parmesan, complete with a fish bone. Only the drinks were satisfactory.

input: Meh is all I can say for TDS. The restaurant itself is just cold.... not literally, but figuratively. There was no decor, no menu boards, stainless steel prep tables as dining tables, no soda machines, staff EVERYWHERE with no identification (shirts, nametags, etc). The food is reasonably priced and most of it was quite good, but what really irked my party was the fact that they charge for extra salsa!!! We ordered a salsa trio (which included 3 samples of the various salsas, in 2oz glass prep bowls), and when my brother asked for more salsa for his tacos (mind you, we ordered one of ever taco, three burritos and guacamole), he was told he'd have to buy the trio again! Really!!??? We spent over $40 on food, drinks and apps, too. Even though the food was decent, I wouldn't return as the atmosphere is just blah and you can't get extra salsa for your damn tacos!
Refine this for me please:
My experience at TDS was, in a word, *meh*. The atmosphere is cold—not in temperature, but in feeling. The space is stark, with no decor or menu boards, and we dined at stainless steel prep tables. Staff were everywhere, yet none wore uniforms or nametags for identification.

While the food is reasonably priced and largely quite good, one policy utterly frustrated our table: they charge for extra salsa. We ordered a salsa trio—three small samples in prep bowls. When my brother requested more for his tacos (after we’d ordered one of every taco, three burritos, and guacamole), we were told he’d need to purchase another full trio. Seriously? After spending over $40 on food, drinks, and appetizers?

The decent food isn’t enough to compensate for the blah atmosphere and the absurdity of not getting extra salsa for your tacos. I won’t be returning.

input: I'm so incredibly happy with our pictures! Angela Clifton Photography have worked with us 3 times and we have been happy with every single picture that was taken! input: Enjoyed my fish out at a sidewalk table.  A bit pricey but food was good.  Go to Side street in French quarter if u want quieter dining outside.

input: The court house is very old and the art is great. The spiral staircase is funny. One can get view of entire city from 5th level. The tower clock room is really surprising with all mechanical gears inside!! You need a prior appointment to get into clock room. Worth spending 2 to 3 hours of time here.
Refine this for me please: The courthouse is ancient and artistically impressive. Its amusing spiral staircase leads to a fifth-level panoramic city view. Most surprising is the tower clock room, filled with mechanical gears—accessible by prior appointment. Allocate two to three hours for a visit; it is thoroughly worthwhile.

input: I had the pleasure to meet with Ann today and not only was she extremely helpful and so positive, she went above and beyond to make my 1st experience here amazing and made it a absolute regular customer from this day forward. Thanks girlie!!
Refine this for me please: It was a pleasure meeting Ann today. She was extremely helpful, positive, and went above and beyond to make my first experience amazing. She has absolutely secured a regular customer from now on. Thanks!

input: This is the first time I tried this place and  I was surprisingly surprised. I had a combination dinner pad Thai and coconut soup. The soup was very tasty as I never had coconut soup before. The pad Thai was exactly what I was expecting and it did not disappoint. The restaurant had great Thai decor and music. The staff and service was top notch. For a town with not much selection for food, this was a great change of pace. This may become my go to place in Carp.
Refine this for me please:
My first visit here was a pleasant surprise. I ordered the combination dinner with pad Thai and coconut soup—both were excellent. The soup offered a new and delicious flavor, while the pad Thai met all my expectations. The authentic Thai decor and music created a lovely atmosphere, complemented by top-notch service. In a town with limited dining options, this restaurant is a wonderful change of pace and may well become my regular spot in Carp.

input: This place was so chill and relaxing. When I come back it'll definitely be in my list if stops. Not to mention the artist performing was fun and eclectic  (I mean really, a country version of "Let It Go", what's not to love?)

input:
Id you haven't been to the Smoothie King center since it was know as the New Orleans Arena, you are in for a nice surprise. The arena has had a face lift and, while the seats are the same,  everything else has been refreshed.   

Most importantly,  the food options are far more varied and appeal to many tastes.  The quality of the food is very good and significantly improved from a few years back. The drink options are much improved as well and include full service bars, spiked lemonade,  bottled and draft beer and of course, smoothies.  There is even a spot for sweets. You can get funnel cake, cotton candy, and all kinds of delicious things I was too full to take in.  

The venue finally feels a bit swanky and top notch.  We are moving on up!
Refine this for me please:
If you haven’t visited the Smoothie King Center since its days as the New Orleans Arena, prepare for a welcome surprise. The venue has undergone a noticeable refresh—while the seating remains familiar, almost everything else feels renewed.

Most notably, the food options are now far more varied and appealing, with significantly improved quality compared to just a few years ago. Drink selections have also expanded to include full-service bars, spiked lemonade, bottled and draft beer, and of course, smoothies. There’s even a dedicated spot for sweets like funnel cake and cotton candy—treats I was too full to try.

Overall, the arena finally carries a swanky, top-tier feel. We’re definitely moving on up!

input: Don't know what it is but If my tummy's feeling icky, I can count on Chipotle's stake to fix me up. I just have to remember not to go during full on lunch time. I usually go between 2 & 4 when it's peaceful and calm. Busy or not the service is always friendly and fast!

input: I must admit, I wasn't expecting much. This place totally blew us away. This has to be one of the best Indian restaurants in the Tampa Bay. Refine this for me please:
I must admit, my expectations were low, but this restaurant completely blew us away. It is easily among the best Indian dining experiences in Tampa Bay. The ambience is wonderful, featuring white tablecloths, but the food is the true star. The Chicken 65 was to die for, and the hot and sour soup was richly flavorful. input:
Had to wait until my third trip to NOLA to actually get in the door.  First two times I tried waiting in line, this time around we got smart and bought reserved seats so we could be on the benches. Well worth the extra $20 to not hassle with waiting in line for an hour. It goes toward the preservation of Jazz so it's a good cause...just splurge.

The show was fantastic.  True musicians and great personalities to boot. I can only imagine that this is what concerts were like 50 years ago. The band members were dapper, engaging and insanely talented.  It's in a tiny hole in the wall space that only holds maybe 200 people? So it's very intimate and nice to see the smiles on the faces of the musicians as they share their craft with you. This is a must do while in NOLA!
Refine this for me please:
It took three trips to New Orleans for me to finally get inside. On my first two attempts, I tried waiting in line. This time, we opted for the smart solution: reserved bench seats for an extra $20. It was well worth avoiding the hour-long queue, and the fee supports jazz preservation—a worthy cause. Just splurge.

The show itself was fantastic. These are true musicians with great personalities, offering a glimpse of what live concerts must have felt like decades ago. The band members were dapper, engaging, and insanely talented. The venue is a tiny hole-in-the-wall, holding perhaps 200 people, creating an intimate setting where you can see the musicians’ smiles as they share their craft. This is an absolute must-do in NOLA.

input: A GREAT EXPERIENCE!!!!!!!!!  I was a completely new customer.  I did not have an appointment because my other plans got rained out and my dealership was too busy to take me.  I needed a PA State & Emissions  inspection which I dread because they can be a total ripoff at some places when they add things on and I just wanted to get it over with.  I saw that this place had much better reviews on Yelp than many other shops in the area.  Keystone Discount Tire took my 2008 Pontiac Torrent in for inspection while I waited and had some free coffee.  I only had to get up once to look at some irregular outer front tire wear on my car when it was on the rack during inspection.  I always appreciate it when the technician lets me look at the problem.   It was nothing major.  Easily correctable with an alignment sometime in the future.  Bill was very friendly, knowledgable, and straightforward with his overall analysis of my car.  My car was fully inspected and stickered in less than an hour without my bill being jacked up with add-ons.   I recommend getting on their mailing list for their coupons!!!!!!!!!!
Refine this for me please:
I was a new customer without an appointment after my other plans fell through. Needing a Pennsylvania State and Emissions inspection, I was dreading the potential for unnecessary upsells. This shop, however, had significantly better reviews than others nearby.

Keystone Discount Tire took my 2008 Pontiac Torrent right in. While I waited with a complimentary coffee, they performed the inspection. The technician even called me over to see some minor irregular wear on a front tire while the car was on the rack—a transparency I always appreciate. He explained it was not urgent and could be corrected with a future alignment.

Bill, who handled my service, was friendly, knowledgeable, and completely straightforward. My car was fully inspected and stickered in under an hour, with no surprise add-ons to the bill. It was a hassle-free, honest experience. I highly recommend them and suggest joining their mailing list for coupons.

input: Wow! I never thought my sons phone could be repaired after he dropped it but it is and it took less than a half an hour! Very professional and excellent service! I'm thrilled!

input: Service and management terrible... After messing up all 4 of our orders the waiter got mad and started cursing... The manager offered our drinks to be free.. What a mess. Refine this for me please: The service and management were appalling. After botching all four of our orders, the waiter became angry and cursed. Though the manager offered free drinks, it was a complete mess. The food was cold and unappetizing; we ate less than half after waiting over an hour. I will never return to Cracker Barrel.

input:
I have been to a number of dog friendly hotels...just not in the city and did not know what to expect. Usually they are motel like.  This one was in the heart of the city.

I walked tentatively into the hotel lobby as i have a labrador/golden mix who is not easy to hide.

We got to the front desk to register and i was still feeling uneasy although my  bf had assured me it was a dog friendly hotel. Reception was so nice immediately putting us at ease. As we checked in an attendant asked if Bentley could have treats which she fullly enjoyed. The Reception person also asked if we would like a welcome kit for Bentley. Holy moly. Of course. Dog dishes, a mat, treats, etc. I was blown away.  

Plus the guests at the hotel all stopped to compliment and pet "queen Bentley". Our room was on the top floor. Awesome!

Even when i went to walk her the car attendants greeted her by name. We were so impressed with the service we decided to come back an extra night. 

Thank you Loews. I didnt realize a hotel could be so dog friendly especially to a big dog.
Refine this for me please:
I have stayed at several dog-friendly hotels before, though never in a city center, so I wasn’t sure what to expect. Typically, they’ve been more like basic motels. This one, however, was located right in the heart of the city.

I entered the lobby a bit tentatively, as I have a large Labrador/Golden Retriever mix who isn’t exactly easy to conceal. My boyfriend had assured me it was dog-friendly, but I still felt uneasy as we approached the front desk. Any worry vanished immediately. The reception staff was wonderfully welcoming, putting us at ease right away. While checking in, an attendant asked if Bentley could have some treats—which she thoroughly enjoyed. The receptionist then offered a welcome kit for her. I was amazed. It included dog bowls, a mat, treats, and more. I was truly blown away.

Even the other guests stopped to compliment and pet “Queen Bentley.” Our room was on the top floor, which was fantastic. Later, when I took her for a walk, the valet attendants greeted her by name. We were so impressed with the service that we decided to extend our stay an extra night.

Thank you, Loews. I never realized a hotel—especially in a city—could be so genuinely welcoming, even to a big dog like Bentley.

input: Sometimes this food is very very good.  Unfortunately it's not consistent.   Ordered something I've been getting for years and every other time it tastes incredible. It's like they have different people in the kitchen and you don't know who you will get. So 50 % of the time it's excellent.  UGH.
Refine this for me please: The food can be excellent, but its quality is inconsistent. An item I’ve ordered for years is incredible only half the time, as if different cooks prepare it. You never know which result you’ll get, which is frustrating.

input:
Been to this location twice and will never go back again!!!!

First time was mediocre, the second time was so very disappointing it beggars belief. I ordered some ribs and had to send them back because one half was warm and the other half was refrigerator cold. They came back and one side was really hot and the other side was still cold, third time it was edible. The manager came over the third time to apologize, never once offered to comp anything. I'm not the kind of guy to cause a fuss to get something comped, but to send something back three times to get it cooked properly and only get an insincere apology really pisses me off, enough for me to write this review.
Refine this for me please: I have visited this restaurant twice and will not return. The first experience was mediocre, but the second was shockingly poor. I ordered ribs and had to send them back because one half was warm and the other was refrigerator-cold. When returned, one side was scalding hot while the other remained cold. Only on the third attempt were they merely edible. The manager came to apologize but never offered to comp the meal. I don’t typically make a fuss for compensation, but having to return a dish three times for proper preparation and receiving only a hollow apology is unacceptable. This frustration compelled me to write this review.

input:
After trying a few ramen places with crazy variety in their selections and stellar broth, I was not too excited about the ramen I got at Cheu.  Maybe it's a matter of taste, but personally, I was not a fan of their thick noodles, and extremely salty broth.  

The service was great, and they had a nice selection of beers!  The friend I went with loved it, and has been many times.  Honestly, I'm just sorry I wasn't a bigger fan.  But I hope others try it for themselves.  I might just be an oddball out on this one.
Refine this for me please:
My recent ramen experiences had set a high bar, with complex broths and variety, so my bowl at Cheu fell short for me. While the service was excellent and the beer selection great, the ramen itself didn’t align with my taste—I found the noodles too thick and the broth excessively salty.

My dining companion, a repeat customer, loved it. I genuinely wish I had enjoyed it more, and I’d still encourage others to try. Perhaps my preference is simply the outlier here.

input:

input:
Looks like there is a second Red Kings restaurant in Chinatown and it did not disappoint! Since this place just opened yesterday, I'm not exactly sure if it's replacing the other Red Kings down the street, or if it is just a second helping of spicy, Szechuan food.

We ordered takeout and picked up the Dan Dan Noodles and a shredded Pork in Garlic sauce dish. The spice level in both dishes was perfect.  Extremely mouth-burning, but with delicious flavors that were sweet, earthy, and fresh. The portions were very generous and will make for great leftovers for us. I can't wait to try some of the other dishes and come back here for a sit-down dinner. They also have karaoke rooms upstairs, plus they are BYOB.
Refine this for me please:
A second Red Kings has opened in Chinatown, and it did not disappoint. It’s unclear whether this new spot replaces the original down the street or simply offers a second helping of spicy Szechuan fare.

We ordered takeout: Dan Dan Noodles and Shredded Pork in Garlic Sauce. The spice level was perfect—intensely mouth-burning yet balanced with sweet, earthy, and fresh flavors. My girlfriends and I chose The Saint in New Orleans for a weekend getaway last year. My first impression was fantastic. The trouble began when my friend arrived and we went out for dinner. We returned to our room laughing, only to be met by a huge flying cockroach. I was horrified. I immediately went to the front desk and insisted they address it. They offered to send maintenance, but that wasn’t good enough for me—where there’s one bold roach, there are always others hiding. input:

My favs are the crab fries, mussels red (white is overloaded with garlic that I can't always take it), the spicy pull and peel shrimp, steamers, and if the mood is right the blue crabs (it's a lot of work but tasty). This place also makes getting down and dirty with your food easy. There are sinks all over so you can rinse the mess off your hands once you're done....good touch.

To sum it up, Chickie's and Pete's is a Philadelphia institution and always a good time. I strongly suggest going at least once to enjoy the experience. 

Please note: Make sure to remember two things before coming during major sporting events. 1. You'll never get a table and 2. You'll deal with a ton of drunk people. I've absolutely been one of these people before and we can get annoying unless you're in the right frame of mind. :)
Refine this for me please:
Chickie’s and Pete’s is the perfect spot to watch the game and indulge. While it may not serve the best food you’ve ever had, if you can snag a seat with a beer, an order of mussels red, and their famous crab fries, you’re guaranteed a great time—whether during a game or any visit near the stadiums.

My personal favorites are the crab fries, mussels red (the white version is overloaded with garlic for my taste), spicy pull-and-peel shrimp, steamers, and, when I’m up for the work, the delicious blue crabs. The restaurant also makes it easy to get messy—there are sinks throughout so you can rinse off afterward, a thoughtful touch.

In short, Chickie’s and Pete’s is a Philadelphia institution and always delivers a fun experience. I strongly recommend going at least once.

A quick heads-up for major sporting events: first, you likely won’t get a table, and second, expect a crowd of enthusiastic, often drunk, fans. Having been one myself, I know we can get a bit annoying—so just come prepared for that energetic atmosphere.

input:
I'm giving this joint 4 stars because they have earned it, but they are definitely 5 star material, if they work out a few kinks. Granted, they just opened, so some of the errors I've experienced (I work in the area, so I've been there several times) will probably get worked out and they are more than willing to make corrections and accommodations when they mess up. 

But over all, the food is REALLY good. Unlike my fellow Yelp-ers, I would say that ther pizza is not their strong suit - its kinds greasy and not sure if they use 100% mozzarella - tastes like its cut with something cheaper. However, so far I've had:  

The Quaker (Chicken version) - Delicious. They make their chicken steaks with the chunky chicken, which I like much more than the shredded version. They could season the chicken more, but the cheese was melted perfectly and the veggies were fresh. 

The fries - crisp and flavorful. I didn't even need ketchup, and I always eat ketchup on my fries

The onion rings - a little greasy, but very tasty and crisp. The onions stayed in the breading and didn't slide out when you bit them (which I hate). 

Spanakopita - mine was a little over cooked, but the flavors were really good

Baklava - VERY GOOD! 

Signature Salad - The veggies they use are very fresh which will make or break a salad. Their balsamic is great too!

The (turkey) Greek Burger - one of the best turkey burgers I've ever had! The patty was moist and flavorful all on its own, but then they top it with what must be homemade tzatziki. I could eat a bowl of that stuff! My burger had romaine instead of the advertised arugula, but it was very fresh, so I didn't mind as much. I also asked for feta, which I didn't get, but that sauce made me forget all about it. 

Overall, this place is great! Provided they don't stray from the high quality standard they are setting, I will keep going back.
Refine this for me please:
I’m giving this spot four stars because they’ve earned it, though they absolutely have the potential to be a five-star establishment once they work out a few kinks. Since they just opened, some of the minor errors I’ve noticed—I work nearby and have visited several times—will likely be resolved. I will say the staff is more than willing to make corrections and accommodations whenever something isn’t right.

Overall, the food is REALLY good. Contrary to some other reviews, I’d argue the pizza isn’t their strong suit—it’s a bit greasy, and the cheese doesn’t taste like pure mozzarella. Almost everything else I’ve tried, however, has been excellent.

The Quaker (chicken version) was delicious. They use a chunky chicken steak, which I prefer over shredded chicken. While the chicken could use more seasoning, the cheese was perfectly melted and the veggies were fresh.

The fries were crisp and so flavorful I didn’t need ketchup—and I always use ketchup. The onion rings were a touch greasy but very tasty and crisp, with the onion staying firmly in the breading when bitten—a pet peeve of mine when it doesn’t.

My spanakopita was slightly overcooked, but the flavors were really good. The baklava was VERY GOOD. Their Signature Salad stood out because of its very fresh vegetables, which make or break a salad, and their balsamic dressing is great.

The turkey Greek Burger was one of the best turkey burgers I’ve ever had. The patty was moist and flavorful on its own, and it was topped with what must be homemade tzatziki sauce—I could eat a bowl of it. My burger came with romaine instead of the advertised arugula, but it was so fresh I didn’t mind. I also didn’t receive the feta I asked for, but that incredible sauce made me forget all about it.

This place is great. Provided they maintain the high standards they’re setting, I’ll definitely keep coming back.

input: Stayed here three nights on business.  The property is located very close to the airport but you really don't hear it.  The rooms are standard TownePlace Suite rooms with a refrigerator, stove, etc..  The area in which the hotel is located is quiet with a combination of other hotels and office buildings.  It's about a 20 minute drive to the downtown or university area.  About 5-10 minutes from Pima Air Museum.  There are not too many restaurants close by but there are some fast food options and a sandwich place called Baggins that was really good and within walking distance.  The staff of the hotel was really friendly and helpful.  The breakfast is standard continental with a couple of hot options. They also have a reception on weekday evenings.  My only complaint is that the food and drink go quickly so get there early.  You could use this as a dinner if you wanted.  I got there about 45 minutes after it started and although there was food left there were very few soft drinks left (no diet).  They could improve by keeping the area stocked throughout the period.  Anyway, the rooms are nice, beds are comfortable and area is safe.
Refine this for me please:
I stayed at this TownePlace Suites for three nights on a business trip. Its location is extremely convenient to the airport, yet aircraft noise is not an issue. The rooms are the brand's standard layout, well-equipped with a refrigerator, stove, and other essentials. The surrounding area is quiet, composed mainly of other hotels and office parks. Downtown and the university are about a 20-minute drive away, while the Pima Air & Space Museum is only 5-10 minutes by car.

Dining options in the immediate vicinity are limited, though there are a few fast-food outlets and an excellent walkable sandwich shop called Baggins. The hotel staff were consistently friendly and helpful. The complimentary breakfast is a standard continental spread with a few hot items, and they host a reception on weekday evenings. My sole suggestion would be for better replenishment of the evening offerings; the food and drinks, particularly diet soft drinks, dwindled quickly. I arrived 45 minutes into the reception to find very few beverages left.

Overall, the rooms are pleasant, the beds are comfortable, and the area feels safe. It’s a solid and practical choice for both business and leisure travelers.
