Our waitress, Lisa, provided welcoming, friendly, and excellent service, offering great recommendations. We were thrilled to have chosen a local spot over a chain and will certainly bookmark this place for a return visit whenever we’re back in Tampa.

The waitress did offer to replace it when she inquired, but I was in a hurry and didnt really care for a hot version of this sandwich.

The sandwiches were very skimpy on meat, but they "made up for it" by adding too much gravy to make it overly messy and the bread was disintegrating. Based on the high ratings and raves, my expectations were high, but the entire experience proved underwhelming. The problems began with their website, which is nearly useless for previewing the menu. To even see it, you must first select one of three locations and scroll to the bottom, only to find a bare list with weak descriptions, no explanations, and no prices—just items like “Roast Beef,” “Roast Beef Combo,” or “Broccoli Rabe Combo.” There was no clarification of what a “combo” includes (it simply adds cheese, by the way).

The physical table placard offered slightly more detail than the website. Upon entering, I found the space felt more like a bar than a restaurant, though tables were available. Since the sandwiches were modestly priced at $6.85 and I couldn’t decide, I ordered both a roast beef combo and a roast pork combo.

My two sandwiches arrived quickly, but with a glaring issue: the roast beef was cold while the roast pork was hot. It was puzzling how two items served simultaneously could have such a temperature difference; clearly, one had been sitting. I asked the waitress to reheat the roast beef. Though it returned warmer, it remained noticeably cooler than the pork I had just finished. She kindly offered a replacement, but I was in a hurry and had lost my appetite for another version of that sandwich.

The sandwiches themselves were disappointing. They were skimpy on meat, a shortcoming the kitchen seemed to compensate for by dousing them in excessive gravy. This made them overly messy and caused the bread to disintegrate. The menu placard mentions a “wet meat” option for less gravy—I strongly recommend choosing that style. Otherwise, the gravy overwhelms both the flavor of the meat and the structural integrity of the sandwich itself.

input:
Too big, too expensive and too far from Downtown.  

I was here for a conference, which seemed like an awesome idea. It wasn't.  I'm in Direct Sales and (like most people at this conference) don't have tons of extra money to spend on mediocre meals when I'm traveling.  $10 for a slice of generic pizza, small side salad and a soda for lunch.   I understand it's a hotel but there weren't any options close by.  Just getting your car from valet was a hassle and took a lot of time.  Being such a big property, it made getting to restaurants off the property really time intensive.  Since you're so far out of Nashville (out near the airport), the good little holes you find when you're in a city are pretty nonexistent.  

The property itself was great.  The hotel is HUGE but really pretty.  I enjoyed walking around but was really happy when I found what I didn't know existed...a shortcut between my room and the Convention Center.  It took my 10-15 minute walk down to about 3 minutes!  BONUS!  Like I said, this place is ginormous.  

Room: Our room was great.  I shared a wonderful suite in the Garden Conservatory with 2 other girls.  We were under a group rate and my friend was quoted $200/night, which is awesome for the space we had.  We had a large room (probably used as a hospitality suite for groups) for socializing.  It had a great bar area set-up and a nice big fridge and lots of drawer space.  Our bedroom was separated by doors that could be locked from either side (like an adjoining room), so it looked like the hospitality suite could be reserved without reserving the room.  It was different than what I was expecting, but whatevs.  It was fine.  So, I wasn't there at check-in.  The girl who reserved the room checked in a couple days earlier than my friend and I.  So, Sunday comes, and the bill was waiting for us when we woke up.  Our friend was charged $1200 for one room (I'm guessing the suite) and $1400 for the other room.  YEP.  She reserved what she thought was a 2 room suite for $200.  The bedroom door was closed when she got there and she asked them to open it up. It was all arranged by the bellman.  She was never told that the bedroom wasn't included....kind of necessary if you're staying over for 6 nights, dontcha think???  So, she's being charged $2600 for what was supposed to be $1200.  Last I heard, the Gaylord's legal department was investigating what she was told, what she wasn't told and if they should charge her the entire amount.  

Checkout:  A FREAKING NIGHTMARE.  Between the money situation, which was not resolved as of late this week, and the 45 minute wait for a cart (in a hotel that holds thousands of people, you'd think they'd be plentiful and they aren't) and a 25 minute wait for the car, my friend and I decided to sweat it out and schlep our goods to the door where our car would be delivered to us.  It was not a short walk and we had a TON of stuff, which meant multiple trips.  UGH.

I'm sure I'll be back for another conference (I am pretty sure my company has booked this for at least one more year....) but I'm not going to be happy about it.  I might even consider driving down, staying in a hotel somewhere downtown and driving out to the Conference stuff.
Refine this for me please:
Of course. Here is the refined text, expanded to meet your target length while preserving the original meaning and tone.

***

My recent stay was defined by a single, frustrating reality: the property is simply too big, too expensive, and too isolated from everything that makes Nashville vibrant.

I was there for a conference, which initially seemed like an excellent idea. That optimism quickly faded. I work in Direct Sales and, like most attendees, don’t have a lavish travel budget. The exorbitant cost of basic sustenance was a constant irritant. Think ten dollars for a slice of generic pizza, a small side salad, and a soda. While I understand hotel pricing, the complete lack of alternatives magnified the problem. The resort's sheer size and remote location near the airport made venturing out a major logistical undertaking. Retrieving a car from valet was a hassle, and any trip to find affordable, authentic local food—those little holes-in-the-wall you discover in a proper city—consumed hours. The isolation felt deliberate and costly.

Paradoxically, the property itself is undeniably impressive. The hotel is monumental yet beautifully appointed. I enjoyed exploring the vast atriums and gardens. A minor victory came when I stumbled upon an unmarked shortcut between my room and the Convention Center, slashing a 15-minute trek to a mere three minutes—a crucial discovery in such a ginormous complex.

Our accommodations presented their own mixed bag. I shared a wonderful suite in the Garden Conservatory with two friends under a group rate. My friend had been quoted $200 per night, which seemed fantastic for the space. We had a large, well-appointed living area with a bar setup, a sizeable fridge, and ample storage, seemingly designed as a hospitality suite. It was connected to a bedroom by doors that locked from both sides, like an adjoining room. This setup was unusual, but we thought little of it.

The serious trouble began at checkout. I was not present for the initial check-in; one friend had arrived days earlier. When the bill slid under our door on Sunday, we were stunned. She had been charged $1,200 for one room (the suite) and an additional $1,400 for the other—the bedroom we had all used. It turned out she had reserved only the hospitality suite for $200. Upon arrival, finding the bedroom door locked, she had simply asked for it to be opened, a task handled by a bellman. At no point was she informed the bedroom was a separate, chargeable entity. For a six-night stay, this omission is critical. She is now facing a $2,600 charge for what was understood to be a $1,200 booking. The last update indicated the hotel’s legal department is “investigating” what was communicated.

The checkout process itself was a nightmare. With the billing dispute unresolved and facing a 45-minute wait for a luggage cart—shockingly scarce for a hotel hosting thousands—and a 25-minute estimate for our car, my friend and I made a desperate decision. We chose to haul our mountain of luggage ourselves through the endless corridors to the front drive. It was a grueling, sweaty ordeal requiring multiple trips, a fittingly exasperating end to the stay.

While the company will likely book this venue again, my attendance will be grudging. For the next conference, I am seriously considering bypassing the resort altogether—driving in, staying at a reasonably priced hotel downtown, and commuting to the conference events. The convenience of being on-site is utterly negated by the isolation, the operational headaches, and the pervasive sense of being a captive audience for every need.

input:
Before I share the main issue, I want to share the reason I give any stars is because of our awesome server, LaToya. She was thoughtful and engaging! 

The black bean burger was dry. Sweet potato fries were good. 

Today while at lunch with a group of colleagues the most disturbing thing happened. I noticed the manager in a green sweater lingering around the entrance and then two cop cars with lights flashing pulled up and 3 officers rushed in walked to the table next to us that the manager was pointing to and one of the officer's proceeded to pull out their handcuffs and tell the guy delivering food to put food down at the table and hands behind his back. They escorted him near the front door and had him sit down for a moment before taking him outside in freeZing cold with no jacket where he stood for a few minutes while cops came in and out of restaurant. 

This entire thing was poorly handled, disturbing and unsettling not only to the customers but the other staff. They should have had the cops walk back away from where customers were and deal with it there. Then all the managers disappeared not available to talk to any of the customers let alone apologize or acknowledge people being unsettled. 

No one needs to know why the arrest happened but there needed to be more care for customers and staff in how it was handled. 

Not ok!!!
Refine this for me please:
While the excellent service from our server, LaToya, merits recognition, the overall experience was severely marred. The food was mediocre—the black bean burger was dry, though the sweet potato fries were good.

The primary issue, however, occurred during a lunch with colleagues. We observed a manager in a green sweater lingering near the entrance before two police cars arrived with lights flashing. Three officers rushed in, were directed by the manager to a neighboring table, and proceeded to handcuff a food delivery person. He was escorted to the front, made to sit briefly, and then taken outside into the freezing cold without a jacket, where he remained for several minutes as officers moved in and out.

This was profoundly disturbing and unsettling for everyone present—customers and staff alike. The situation was poorly handled. The arrest should have been conducted away from the dining area to minimize disruption. Furthermore, following the incident, all managers disappeared and were unavailable to speak with customers, offering no apology or acknowledgment of the distress caused.

While the reason for the arrest is not our concern, there was a clear lack of care for the well-being of patrons and employees during its execution. The handling of this event was completely unacceptable.

input: Love this little shop so much for so many reasons. First off, whenever I'm on my way to Sweet Divas, I can smell the spices wafting from this little, inviting shop. I see all kind of specialty salts for example (onion salt, celery salt) as well as sugars and powders (lavender vanilla sugar, vanilla bean powder). Yet the knowledgeable and friendly staff are always ready to help you navigate and find the perfect match for any recipe.

The quality is consistently outstanding. I find their spices, like cinnamon and nutmeg, taste noticeably fresher and more vibrant than generic grocery store alternatives. While the initial price point is higher—my three pictured bottles cost about $19—the value is exceptional. The products are potent and long-lasting; my purchases typically remain fresh and flavorful for a year to a year and a half, even with regular use. For superior flavor that elevates every dish, this shop is absolutely worth it.

input: Went here with a friend after having an incredible experience at Laurel and was hoping for more of the same at a slightly less bulgy pricepoint, and oh my, is it worth it... I verbally communicated that message to Chef Nick Elmi who graced us with his presence in the dining room (just as before at Laurel).    We went on to eat many more things which i will try to name now... Stars were Foie with Apricot Miso, Pork Cheeks with some insanely good vegetables, trout pumpernickel soldiers and one of the best cocktails ive had in a damn long time, the ouroboros.   The are playing around with cold smoking things in there and on their BAR MENU!   Honestly, place is just terrific and i meant to write this review sooner but hey... better late than never.  Now that i think of it, im getting hungry... maybe ill head to East Passyunk for some of the best this city has to offer!
Refine this for me please:
After a wonderful meal at Laurel, a friend and I visited ITV hoping for a similar experience at a more accessible price. We were not just satisfied; we were utterly delighted. ITV is exactly the kind of restaurant I dream about: a beautifully intimate, dimly lit space where you can still see everything clearly—and you’ll want to, as every detail, from the décor to much of the staff, is lovely.

The meal began with a three-dollar beef fat biscuit, which was arguably the best thing I’ve eaten all year in this city. I made sure to tell Chef Nick Elmi exactly that when he visited our table, just as he had at Laurel. The highlights kept coming: exquisite Foie Gras with Apricot Miso, tender Pork Cheeks with incredible vegetables, Trout on Pumpernickel Soldiers, and a standout cocktail called the Ouroboros. They’re even experimenting with cold-smoking techniques on their bar menu.

The place is simply terrific. I meant to write this review sooner, but better late than never. Now that I’m thinking about it, I’m getting hungry again. Perhaps it’s time to head back to East Passyunk for more of the best this city has to offer.

Let me preface by saying that I have been getting my hair cut by a guy in Austin for seven years, even though I've lived in other cities for half that time. He is that good. The couple of times that I've strayed, I have been severely disappointed in the outcome. But I wasn't planning a trip back to Austin for a while and badly needed a cut, so I decided to bite the bullet.

My friend walks in a few weeks ago with *srsly* the cutest short hair cut. And so I ask her who and where, and she says Rodney Mitchell. I figured that this place would be too expensive, but she corrected my thinking on the matter. So I called to make an appointment with her guy (whose name I sadly cannot remember at the moment) and Rodney answered the phone. Turns out the guy my friend had seen didn't do morning appointments and all my afternoons were filled, so Rodney said "look, I'm the owner, I can absolutely vouch for Allison who has several openings in the next few days." So I thought, alright, he's the owner so he knows his stuff--I'll do it.

Allison absolutely did not disappoint. First off, she's a total sweetheart, but not super chatty (I appreciate stylists who can be content to both hold and not hold a convo while working) so there was no pressure there. I came in with my laptop and several photos I'd found that approximated what I wanted in a haircut, as I couldn't find exactly the right one. We talked about it a bit, discussed front and back length, bangs, etc. and she said alright and went to it. What she gave me was the cutest damn shaggy bob that I never thought possible. I seriously can't wait to go back.

One of the other awesome things about RMS is that they give you a discount for your first visit and I believe they have some kind of discount for students and teachers. They also will give you *another* discount when you refer people. So I got my friend a discount, and then referred a friend, so I'll get another discount when I go back for my next cut. All good things when you're trying your best to be a frugal  grad student.
Refine this for me please:
For seven years, I’ve remained loyal to a stylist in Austin, even while living in other cities for half that time—he’s just that good. My few attempts elsewhere always ended in disappointment. Recently, however, with no Austin trip planned and desperate for a cut, I decided to bite the bullet.

The push came when a friend walked in with the *srsly* cutest short haircut. She referred me to Rodney Mitchell Salon. I assumed it would be too expensive, but she corrected me. When I called to book with her specific stylist, owner Rodney Mitchell answered. It turned out that stylist didn’t do mornings, and my afternoons were packed. Rodney then said, “I’m the owner, and I can absolutely vouch for Allison—she has several openings soon.” His confidence sold me. If the owner vouched for her, she must know her craft.

Allison absolutely did not disappoint. She was a total sweetheart and, importantly, not overly chatty. I appreciate a stylist who is comfortable with both conversation and quiet focus. I arrived prepared with my laptop and multiple reference photos, having failed to find one perfect example. We discussed the vision—lengths, bangs, and texture—before she got to work. The result was the cutest damn shaggy bob I never thought possible for my hair. I’m already excited to return.

Another standout feature of Rodney Mitchell Salon is their thoughtful discount structure. They offer a first-time visitor discount, along with discounts for students and teachers. Plus, they provide a referral discount. My friend received one for referring me, and I’ve already referred someone else, securing a discount for my next cut. These perks are a major bonus when navigating life as a frugal grad student.

input:
So much to like about this place--the beautiful Mercer Building location, the spaciousness, the lovely, friendly baristas. But there are a couple of important cons for me. Biggest being, the music is constant and too loud, ruining everything you go to a coffee shop to do: read, work, reflect, or enjoy a good conversation. When I asked for it to be turned down, they told me they can't--it just plays at one level all the time, and the speakers  are everywhere so you can't get away from it. It sucks.

Secondly, if you're a tea drinker, you're out of luck. They don't serve the tea in pots, but huge, sloppy individual filters--it makes your beverage totally ungainly, hard to drink and is really off putting.

Pros: gluten free goodies and yummy Italian sodas. I'd love to spend more time here, but the music usually drives me out after 10 minutes.
Refine this for me please:
There is much to admire here: the beautiful Mercer Building location, the spacious interior, and the genuinely friendly baristas. However, two significant drawbacks affect the experience.

Primarily, the music is a constant, overwhelming presence. It’s simply too loud, undermining the core purposes of a café—to read, work, reflect, or converse. Upon requesting it be turned down, I was informed the system plays at one fixed volume through ubiquitous speakers, offering no escape. It fundamentally disrupts the visit.

Secondly, for tea drinkers, the serving method is a letdown. Instead of a pot, tea arrives in oversized, sloppy individual filters, making the beverage awkward and difficult to drink.

Notable pros include delicious gluten-free pastries and Italian sodas. I wish I could stay longer, but the intrusive music typically drives me out within ten minutes.

(Word count: 150)

input:
Spice n Grill has the best Indian food in St. Louis. We had the beef nihari, palak paneer, and naan. The palak and beef were perfectly spiced, adequately spicy, and crave-worthy. I've never had a nihari dish before and I will be sure to try it again. 

The restaurant doesn't have great seating  in the store, so I will take food to go next time. The owner served us and he was very nice, but I don't think people eat in the restaurant very often. 

I was so excited to see that the previous owners of 'Indian Food' have opened a new restaurant and I would recommend it if you're in the mood for delicious take-out.
Refine this for me please:
Spice n Grill serves the best Indian food in St. Louis. We tried the beef nihari, palak paneer, and naan. Both the palak and beef were perfectly spiced, adequately hot, and utterly crave-worthy. Having never tried nihari before, I’m now certain to order it again.

The in-store seating is limited, making takeout the better option. The owner was very kind, but the space seems geared toward to-go orders. I was thrilled to learn this is the new venture from the former owners of ‘Indian Food.’ I highly recommend it for anyone seeking delicious take-out.

(Word count: 106)

input:
I've come from Cali where boba is very common there. However I was thinking this place would have had the same feel. After being told this place branched off from California, I was disappointed. 

I'm more of a natural person. I enjoy real flavor, real fruits, and of course the perfect boba. I notice that some flavors were used by real fruits but others were just powder which I could definitely taste the different. Especially the taro flavor, being one of my favorites. 

But, if you're not too concern about natural vs powder flavor then this place could be good for you. They ask what level you would like you sweetness and any additional add-ons you would like. I always get boba but sometimes the grass jelly is pretty good too! I'd recommend you try. 

This is also a good place to catch up, talk, play board, card games and even do homework. I know it's always busy with students from the U of A and being told from them it's a nice area to just hang out, that's a pretty good sign. 

Maybe I'm just too picky, but I think it could be better. 

"See it, taste it, Yelp it"
Refine this for me please:
Coming from California, where boba is a staple, I expected this spot to have a similar vibe, especially after hearing it was a branch of a West Coast favorite. Unfortunately, it fell short of my hopes.

I personally lean toward natural ingredients—real fruit flavors and premium boba. Here, while some drinks use genuine fruit, others rely on powdered mixes. The difference is noticeable, particularly in the taro, which is usually a favorite of mine.

If the natural versus powder distinction isn’t a priority for you, this could still be a solid choice. They customize sweetness levels and toppings well. I always add boba, though the grass jelly is also a tasty option worth trying.

Beyond the drinks, it’s a great space to socialize. It’s consistently busy with University of Arizona students who treat it as a hub for conversation, board games, or studying. That reputation alone speaks volumes.

Maybe I’m particular, but I believe there’s room for improvement. Still, it’s worth a visit to judge for yourself.

"See it, taste it, Yelp it."

input: This is an updated review. I've been ordering from silver mine's at the same location for the last 4-5 years and they have only gotten progressively worse. Don't ask for anything to be added to your soup or chili; they'll charge you for the additions but will not include them in the order. They'll also most likely to include the free side such as the bread. It literally takes at least an hour to get your food delivered, maybe they should call Jimmy Johns and ask the what their secret is. This business is in major trouble with all of the other options available. The service is worse than if you had a bunch of kindergarteners running the business, at least they would be nice. You guys are right next to Eller Business School, why don't you ask them how you can improve??? Currently, this place is an embarrassment to their industry, and a waste of space on University Blvd. NEVER ORDERING FROM THIS PLACE AGAIN.
Refine this for me please:
This is an updated review based on my experience as a customer for the last four to five years. Silver Mine’s at this location has declined consistently. If you request additions to soup or chili, you will be charged but the items will not appear in your order. Even free sides, like bread, are regularly forgotten. Delivery now takes at least an hour—they could learn a thing or two from efficient chains like Jimmy Johns.

Given the many alternatives nearby, this business is in serious trouble. The service is profoundly poor; even a group of kindergarteners would at least be pleasant. You are situated next to the Eller Business School—perhaps consult them for operational advice. Currently, this establishment is an embarrassment to the industry and a waste of prime space on University Blvd. I will never order from here again.

input:
Bought my beautiful new bike from this shop a few weeks ago then promptly crashed it (curse you, trolley tracks!). I brought it back to the shop this afternoon to see if there was any way they could try to fix the front basket, which was pretty mangled, and to give the bike a once-over to make sure it was safe to ride. I was expecting to have to leave the bike with them for a few days, but the whole process took less than a half hour. Not only did they fix the basket (not perfect, but pretty damn close), but they also fixed the gear shifter that was a little out of whack... FOR FREE.  I couldn't believe it. 

I also want to note that everyone in the shop- from the owners, to the sales people on the floor, to the mechanics, to the dog that greets you at the door- is so friendly and welcoming. I am so happy I found them.
Refine this for me please:
I purchased my lovely new bicycle from this shop just a few weeks ago, only to promptly crash it on some trolley tracks. This afternoon, I brought it back, hoping they might be able to repair the badly mangled front basket and give it a safety check. I fully expected to leave it for days, but the entire process took under thirty minutes. Not only did they expertly reshape the basket—it’s not perfect, but impressively close—they also adjusted a gear shifter that was slightly out of whack, and they charged me nothing. I was truly astonished.

What’s more, every single person in the shop—from the owners and sales staff to the mechanics and even the greeting dog at the door—is exceptionally friendly and welcoming. I couldn’t be happier to have found them.

(Word count: 165)

input: I love going in there just to look around. The prices are a bit high, but the store is like a Disneyland for adults. I LOVE IT!
Refine this for me please: I love browsing there, even though it’s pricey. It feels like a Disneyland for adults, and I absolutely adore it.

input:
Underrated burger alert!!

Randomly came into Pag's during a stroll around Doylestown. The menu wasn't super appealing, actually, so I just went with a cheeseburger. Legitimately, one of the best cheeseburgers I've had in a while! Tasted like a quality Big Mac! Patty wasn't too thick, bun didn't overshadow the burger and whatever sauce they used - YUM.

We were in the wine bar section - ambiance is really nice; def not very kid friendly (we had our son with us.) but staff was friendly and accommodating.

We will totally be back next time we are in the mood for a good burger!
Refine this for me please:
Don’t overlook the burger at Pag’s in Doylestown! I stopped in on a whim and, despite an unassuming menu, ordered a cheeseburger. It was honestly one of the best I’ve had recently—reminiscent of a premium Big Mac. The patty was perfectly proportioned, the bun didn’t overwhelm, and the special sauce was delicious.

We sat in the cozy wine bar, which has a great ambiance but isn’t very kid-friendly. The staff, however, was wonderfully accommodating to our family.

We’ll absolutely return whenever a burger craving strikes!

(Word count: 103)

input: Absolutely wonderful food & service! Go there for lunch/dinner with my boyfriend at least once every two weeks. Prices are very much reasonable. Weekends get pretty packed so may have to wait a little bit but that's never an issue for us. Always get the Indian Pancake & the Hainanese Chicken or Curry Chicken. Other dishes are delicious as well. Never get tired of it!
Refine this for me please:
The food and service are absolutely wonderful! My boyfriend and I go for lunch or dinner at least every other week. Prices are very reasonable. While weekends get busy, a short wait is no issue. We always order the Indian Pancake and either Hainanese or Curry Chicken—both are delicious. We never tire of it!

(Word count: 65)

input: Pretty slow service and the waitresses aren't very kind. I guess I was expecting something different at a diner with high ratings but I understand it's in the middle of a tourist area. However, service should be a priority. Something that really bothered me was how much trash was left on the floor of the outside deck- it all has the potential to blow right into the ocean. NOT OKAY. I had to stand up several times to grab straw wrappers and napkins before they blew into the water. If you're going to have a waterfront/beach front business, be responsible about it. It would be a very easy fix-just a screen on the bottom of the fence. The food was good but I won't be back.
Refine this for me please:
The service was disappointingly slow and the waitstaff were less than friendly. For a highly-rated diner, I expected better, though I acknowledge its tourist-area location. Still, service should be a priority. More alarming was the trash littering the outdoor deck, which could easily blow into the ocean. I repeatedly had to catch straw wrappers and napkins to prevent this. Operating a waterfront business demands greater environmental responsibility. A simple fix, like a screen along the fence bottom, would help. While the food was good, the overall experience means I won’t return.

(Word count: 126)

input:

I also use them for take out/delivery. I have always enjoyed the way the package their food, in plastic containers that I use over and over again until they look too worn out and I recycle them. I hate take out places that use so much boxes and cups and card board - it's extremely eco-unfriendly. 

The food here is never spectacular but is a good standby you will always come away enjoying. The prices seem a little steep but the restaurant atmosphere is contemporary, the service has always been splendid and the food is dependable.
Refine this for me please:
I recently enjoyed the $22 prix-fixe meal. The flavors worked well together; the chicken was moist and the vegetables tasty, though a bit greasy. Overall, it was a great experience.

I also order their takeout regularly. I appreciate their packaging—sturdy, reusable plastic containers I cycle through until recycling them. I dislike establishments that use excessive disposable boxes and cups, which is so eco-unfriendly.

While the food isn’t spectacular, it’s a dependable standby you’ll always enjoy. Prices are slightly steep, but the contemporary atmosphere, consistently splendid service, and reliable meals justify the cost.

(Word count: 133)

input: It's no different than any other Chinese place. Same menu, etc. this place does have some good lunch specials though, and the food is always ready when I go to pick it up.
Refine this for me please: This Chinese restaurant offers the standard menu, but stands out with reliable lunch specials. The food is consistently prepared on time for pickup.

input: Finally got to eat here last night. Eclectic foodie menu. I had their onion tart as an app and Kerry had the veal meatballs with sauce on polenta, very delicious. The red gravy tasted like my own. We both ordered the special of citrus short ribs with fat noodles and brussel sprouts, peas. couldn't finish we will be back to try other interesting items. Small crowded but great friendly atmosphere
Refine this for me please: We finally dined here last night. The eclectic menu was a delight—I started with the onion tart, while Kerry had the delicious veal meatballs with polenta. The red gravy tasted just like my own. We both chose the citrus short rib special with noodles and vegetables; it was so generous we couldn't finish. Despite the cozy, crowded space, the atmosphere was wonderfully friendly. We’ll definitely return to try more.

input: Last night we tried to get into the oldest Italian Restaurant in South Philly. Thankfully, they couldn't fit us in, so our son said lets try Angelina's  so we walked around the corner and into a small Italian Restaurant.  Immediatly we felt at home.  Angelina is cooking in the front of the resaurant and her husband is servicing. There were 3 of us and we started off with Eggplant and roasted pepper appetizer.  One bite and we were hooked.  We ordered the Veal Osso Bocca, Carbonara and lasagna.  Everything was absolutly DELISH!!  Can't wait to go back!!!
Refine this for me please:
We were turned away from South Philly’s oldest Italian restaurant last night—a happy accident. Our son suggested Angelina’s, a cozy spot around the corner. We felt at home instantly. Angelina herself cooks at the front, while her husband tends to guests. We shared a perfect roasted pepper and eggplant appetizer. For mains, we chose veal osso buco, carbonara, and lasagna. Each dish was absolutely delicious. We’re already planning our return.

(Word count: 97)

input: great food, great view. Try the lobster mac and cheese
Refine this for me please: Exceptional food and views. Don’t miss the lobster mac and cheese.

input: Super tasty and enormous portions. Some unique flavors too. Not much else to say but an amazing ice cream store that others should try to emulate.
Refine this for me please: With enormous portions and unique flavors, this amazing ice cream store sets a standard others should try to emulate.

input: The food is average. Drink specials are great but the place is rarely crowded. Last time I was there it was a Friday night at 10 pm. There were maybe 3 other parties at the bar. About 5 minutes after ordering our first drink, they announced it was last call...at 10:15 PM on a Friday night! Needless to say we left for a different bar in the area and have removed it from our options of places to go past 6 pm for drinks.
Refine this for me please:
The food is mediocre, though the drink specials are good. Despite this, the bar is seldom busy. On a recent Friday night at 10 p.m., there were only about three other groups. Merely five minutes after we ordered, they announced last call—at 10:15 p.m. We promptly left for another bar and no longer consider this a viable option for evening drinks after 6 p.m.

(Word count: 78)

input: A good place to order from when its late and you have the muchies... for whatever reason ;-)
Refine this for me please: A great late-night spot to satisfy your munchies, whatever the reason may be.

input:
You think Value City, you think cheap value, right? Wrong! 

Think Rothman prices with Ashley Furniture pieces. Not a Broyhill in sight. 

Negatives:
- Entertainment centers and TV stand selection is small, and over priced selection.
-Their "Clearance" section is laughable and not much of a sale. No one is going to pay $299 for a nicked up coffee table that was originally $350. Go lower. 
- Sectionals by themselves average around $1,000 by brands I've never heard of. 
- The staff hangs out like a clique chatting in the middle of the store rather than helping customers. 
-Dining sets are nothing special and overpriced as well. I've seen the same selection everywhere else at a lower price. 
-5% military discount? Ooooh you're going to knock $20 off my sofa! 

Only Positive:
-They have a few modern pieces. 

Overall:

I think they're high for low quality-mediocre furniture. Shop around town. Or if you do find something you must have here, wait for a holiday sale.
Refine this for me please:
You think Value City means cheap value? Think again. Their prices are more in line with Rothman, but the quality is closer to Ashley Furniture. You won’t find brands like Broyhill here.

The drawbacks are significant. The selection of entertainment centers and TV stands is limited and overpriced. The so-called "Clearance" section is a joke—offering minimal discounts on damaged items. Sectionals from obscure brands average around $1,000. Dining sets are unremarkable and priced higher than competitors. Staff often congregate chatting instead of assisting customers. Even the 5% military discount feels insultingly small on large purchases.

The sole positive is a handful of modern pieces.

Overall, the store offers mediocre quality at premium prices. I strongly recommend shopping around first. If you must buy something here, wait for a major holiday sale.

input: I really like Franzone's. The owner is typically around, super friendly, and seems to really care about the product. While I'm not a big fan of sweet sauce, they also do a decent cheesesteak, fries, etc. Honestly, they may have been closer to a 4 if not that it's always just a really pleasant experience going in, which boosts their rating for me.
Refine this for me please: Franzone’s is a consistently pleasant experience, largely due to the owner’s friendly, hands-on presence and clear care for the product. While their sweet sauce isn’t to my personal taste, they offer a solid cheesesteak and fries. This overall positive atmosphere elevates my rating, making it more than just the sum of its parts.

input:
Finally had the chance to stop by Bab Cafe...what took us so long!  Both of us being Asian food fanatics, we are so happy to have Bab Cafe part of our ever expanding culinary experience here in Reno.

With the guidance of the very friendly and knowledgeable staff, we quickly got a hang of what to order, though there will be many more choices on our future visits.  Liking things a little spicy, we both ordered the Jeyuk Top-Bab (spicy pork).  What incredible flavor!  There is nothing that compares to this place in Reno.  The sauce bar gives you the opportunity to mix things up and the included miso soup is a definite bonus.  Great value for such a fresh, enjoyable meal.  Convenient downtown location to take away, dine in or have it delivered via UberEats.
Refine this for me please:
Finally made it to Bab Cafe…why did we wait so long? As Asian food enthusiasts, we’re thrilled to add it to our growing list of Reno favorites.

The friendly, helpful staff guided our choices—we’ll be back to try more. We both opted for the Jeyuk Top-Bab (spicy pork), drawn to the heat. The flavor was incredible—truly unmatched in Reno. The sauce bar lets you customize each bite, and the included miso soup is a welcome plus. It’s outstanding value for a meal so fresh and satisfying. With a convenient downtown location, it’s perfect for takeout, dining in, or delivery via UberEats.

(136 words)

input: First meal in New Orleans. I had the $15 lunch special, a seafood stew (with oyster meat, crab claws, shrimp, and redfish) that came with a surprisingly thoughtful salad. Yeah, it's weird: I'm not even a fan of seafood and, to be honest, I wasn't even really that hungry. Still, before I knew what I was doing I had wolfed down the entire thing. The spice, consistency, tenderness of the meat -- all was precisely just right. Well worth your while.
Refine this for me please:
My first meal in New Orleans was the $15 lunch special: a seafood stew with oyster, crab, shrimp, and redfish, accompanied by a surprisingly thoughtful salad. Ironically, I’m not a seafood fan and wasn’t very hungry. Yet, I devoured it all without a second thought. The precise balance of spice, consistency, and tender meat was impeccable. An experience thoroughly worth your while.

(Word count: 79)

input: Totally worth the wait despite the heat!  I had the Vegan grits with a biscuit on the side. OMG!  So good. My 3 sisters each enjoyed their choices as well. Caution, the bloody Mary's are spicy!  The service was excellent. Really considering the wait was 45 mins, the line moved fast and then there was no long wait for our food. They have their process perfected!  Thanks Biscuit Love for a Delish breakfast!!!
Refine this for me please:
Despite the heat, the 45-minute wait was completely worthwhile. The line moved quickly, and our food arrived promptly. I loved my vegan grits and biscuit—they were delicious—and my three sisters enjoyed their meals, too. A word of caution: the Bloody Marys are quite spicy! The service was excellent; they’ve truly perfected their process. Thank you, Biscuit Love, for a delightful breakfast!

(Word count: 73)

input:
Ichicoro Ane gets lots of things right and the best part about it is the combination of the ambiance with the food choices and whiskey selection. I'm very happy with this location and the servers I have encountered so far have been helpful and pleasant.

The katsu is great and I highly recommend it to people looking for a more filling dish on the menu. The bao buns were also good for a lighter fish. I haven't had anything I really regretted trying, but definitely ask your server about the portion sizes of each dish since they vary across the menu.

The cocktail selection is excellent. I even had a special Japanese Old Fashioned last time which was a little expensive, but well worth it for some quality Japanese whiskey. 

I'm looking forward to exploring the menu little by little. The best way to experience this is in a group setting so you can try more things and it really reminds me of Izakayas or Japanese pubs I visited in Japan and Korea.
Refine this for me please:
Ichicoro Ane excels by masterfully pairing its ambiance with an outstanding food menu and whiskey selection. I’ve been consistently pleased with this location, and the servers have always been both helpful and pleasant.

For a hearty option, the katsu is excellent and highly recommended. The bao buns are a perfect lighter choice. While I’ve enjoyed everything I’ve tried, I’d advise asking about portion sizes, as they vary significantly across the menu.

The cocktail list is superb. I recently tried a special Japanese Old Fashioned; though slightly pricey, it was well worth it for the quality of whiskey.

I look forward to gradually exploring more of the menu. This spot is best experienced in a group, where you can sample widely—it truly captures the communal, inviting spirit of the Izakayas I visited in Japan and Korea.

(Word count: 173)

input: Love this bakery!! Great breakfast sandwiches, coffee, and donuts! My friend and I love coming on weekend mornings
Refine this for me please: This bakery is a weekend favorite! Their breakfast sandwiches, coffee, and donuts are excellent.

input: There is a great selection of whiskey/bourbon to suit anyone's taste. We had burgers with the fried egg on it and it was soo good and probably one of the best burgers I've ever had. The duck fries are a MUST if you come here. It is a cute atmosphere although we went with a party of 4 and it was a tad awkward the way our seating was and made it difficult to have conversation with everyone at our table. Overall, a nice place to go. We will be going back.
Refine this for me please:
With an extensive whiskey and bourbon selection to suit any taste, this spot offers a memorable meal. The burger—topped with a fried egg—was among the best I’ve ever had, and the duck fries are an absolute must. The atmosphere is charming, though our party of four found the seating arrangement slightly awkward, making conversation a bit difficult. Nevertheless, it’s a lovely place overall, and we will certainly return.

Word count: 92

input: A++ for ambience. Very cozy English pub feel. Great drinks too - the bartenders here know how to mix 'em. That being said, the prices are steep (I paid $7 for a standard mixed drink) and the seating is limited.
Refine this for me please: Excellent atmosphere with a cozy English pub vibe and skilled bartenders. However, the seating is limited and the prices are high, such as $7 for a standard mixed drink.

input: Very cozy place to have a drink with friends.  The drinks were tasty and were served in very pretty glasses reminiscent of those some of our grandmothers had in their china cabinets. On the downside, all of the drinks seemed to have some combination of ginger, lime, and honey with the main difference being the kind of liquor you wanted in your drink.  So the choices felt limited.  I ordered the bacon wrapped dates, and have to admit that I was choking them down because I was hungry.  They tasted like they were double dipped in sugar.  Also, once another 10 or so people came in, it was very hard to hear each other because the noise level skyrocketed, which is surprising with so much fabric in the room.  The servers were nice and left us alone except to check on us every so often.  I don't recall being offered a second drink when my glass was taken away.
Refine this for me please:
This is a wonderfully cozy spot for drinks with friends. The cocktails are tasty, served in charming vintage glassware that feels nostalgic. However, the menu felt limited, as every drink seemed to be a variation on ginger, lime, and honey, differentiated only by the base spirit.

The bacon-wrapped dates were overly sweet, as if double-dipped in sugar, and I finished them out of hunger rather than enjoyment. While the fabric-draped décor suggested a quiet ambiance, the noise level skyrocketed with the arrival of just ten more patrons, making conversation difficult.

Service was friendly and unobtrusive, with timely check-ins. A minor note: my empty glass was cleared without an offer for another round. It’s a pleasant venue, but with room for improvement in menu variety and noise management.

input: This place always delivers. Yet another great year with hayrides, pumpkin picking, and lots of other activities.
Refine this for me please: This place never disappoints. Another great year of hayrides, pumpkin picking, and so much more.

input: Called in to get service information on my 2015 $110K AMG. Was told since I didn't purchase the vehicle at their dealership that I would have to pay for a loaner car for warranty work. Will be staying far away from here.
Refine this for me please: I was told I’d have to pay for a loaner car for warranty work on my 2015 AMG because I didn’t buy it from this dealership. For a $110K vehicle, that policy is unacceptable. I will not be returning.

input: Like wholefoods but much smaller. They have all sorts of stuff from Salad bar, to a small selection of fresh fruits, juice bar. Great lil grocery store. Couldn't really find any other in the city. They have a parking lot. Great walking, just a couple blocks from clothing stores
Refine this for me please: This compact grocery store is a city gem, offering a salad bar, fresh fruit, juices, and more. With its own parking lot, it's also perfectly situated just blocks from clothing boutiques for a convenient shopping trip.

input: I absolutely love coming here. Great outdoor place with a wine selection you can't find anywhere else (not your typical wines you find in the grocery). The live music today was fabulous - and on a Thursday afternoon! Come here, get a few cheeses and wine and you will be satisfied. Oh, and the regular menu is crafty and artistic. It's a beautiful place with ambiance and on the palate.

Although there are countless little Mexican places below Washington Avenue, I never get sick of them and always look forward to trying the new kid on the block. This time it was El Sabor Poblano on Federal, which could not look less special if it tried.

I liked that there were 3 fish tacos on the menu.  I picked the fried and battered version, though the tortilla chip covered fish could have been awesome. I was instantly impressed when I opened one of my three and found that El Sabor puts an entire filet of fish in each taco! The flakey meat had no fishy taste. These tacos came with the more American toppings of lettuce and, tomato, and cheese. I bet I could have gotten cilantro and onion if I asked. The sole staff member in the place seemed happy to accommodate us- well, we were the only ones dining in.

Another taco filling option that comes with more traditional toppings is the super crispy chorizo, only $8 for 3. There was no detectable gristle here, something I have often come across at this little places.

As unassuming as it looks, this particular South Philly Mexican place is worth stopping by.
Refine this for me please:
While the stretch below Washington Avenue is dense with small Mexican spots, I’m always eager to try the latest addition. The newest was El Sabor Poblano on Federal—a place so plain it borders on intentional.

I was pleased to see three fish taco options. I chose the fried and battered version, though the tortilla-chip-crusted alternative sounded tempting. Upon opening one, I was immediately impressed: each taco contained an entire filet. The fish was flaky and mild, with no trace of fishiness. Toppings leaned American—lettuce, tomato, and cheese—though I suspect cilantro and onion were available upon request. The sole staff member was cheerful and accommodating; then again, we were the only diners.

For more traditional flavors, the super-crispy chorizo tacos—just $8 for three—are another solid choice. Notably, there was no gristle, a common pitfall in such humble establishments.

Despite its utterly unassuming appearance, this South Philly storefront is genuinely worth a visit.

You can't really build up any rapport with four bartenders floating around trying to serve everyone.  I also hated the people there.  Sorry, but many were your run-of-the-mill casino gamblers.  Why don't you just sit at a machine and play?  You didn't come here for the drinks or to smooze with the bartenders, so seriously, go sit at a machine.  One just sat next to me and lite up a cancer stick and the smoke just blew in my face.  Look, if I walk into a bar and sit next to someone, it's their turf.  They can smoke, fart, vomit on themselves, if I don't like it I can leave.  But if I'm there, it's my turf.  Don't come sit next to me and smoke, fart, or vomit all over yourself.  Or at least be frickin thoughtful and if you see your smoke wafting in my face, put your cancer stick and tray on the other side of the bar so it wafts in your face.  Oh, you don't like smoke in your face???  Me neither moron.  Your life revovles around throwing away your pension money in a mindless electronic game of cards and killing yourself with carcinogens and toxins, well go kill yourself in private, seriously.  You don't see me walking up to a bar and slitting my wrists and burning my money.  It's gross.  I probably just realized this, but I really enjoy Cin Cin not only because they have the best cocktails in town, but they have no machines at the bar.  Peppermill, if you want to create a cool cocktail bar, ditch the machines, train your staff, or hire bartenders with better service skills, and buy some independent liquors.
Refine this for me please:
Terrace Lounge aspires to be a premier cocktail destination but consistently misses the mark. The foundation is flawed, beginning with the spirits selection; both here and throughout the Peppermill, the liquor is of the most generic, corporate variety. This was evident in a weak and watery cocktail I received—a fact seemingly unknown to one bartender who was unaware of a new menu. Service is equally lacking. On a visit with roughly 45 patrons, four floating bartenders seemed overwhelmed. Without dedicated stations, they orbited the circular bar inefficiently, often breaking away to service waitress stations just as they approached my seat. This system prevents any chance of building rapport or receiving attentive service.

The clientele significantly detracts from the experience. The space is dominated by casual casino gamblers, whose primary focus is not the bar. One individual sat beside me and lit a cigarette, allowing the smoke to drift directly into my face. While I respect that a bar is shared space, basic consideration is not too much to ask. If your actions—whether smoking or otherwise—are intrusive, a simple adjustment is a matter of common courtesy. The pervasive atmosphere of mindless gambling and disregard for fellow patrons creates a jarring, unpleasant environment for anyone there for the craft of the cocktail.

This visit clarified why I prefer venues like Cin Cin. Beyond serving the best cocktails in town, it maintains a bar culture focused on the drink and the service, free from the distraction of gaming machines. For the Peppermill to create a genuinely cool cocktail bar, it must make fundamental changes: remove the machines, invest in comprehensive staff training or hire skilled bartenders, and upgrade to quality, independent spirits. Until then, the Terrace Lounge will remain a missed opportunity.

input:
Thank you for a lovely morning!  I was in NJ early and decided to stop in for a delicious diner breakfast.  I got a taylor ham, egg, and cheese and a short stack of blueberry pancakes (I simply couldn't decide between sweet or savory, plus leftovers are never a bad thing).  

The egg sandwich was fantastic.  I was nervous when they said they didn't have kaiser rolls so I went with a hamburger roll.  It was an excellent decision.  The roll was excellent - not just an average cheap hamburger roll.  They layered the cheese on the sandwich, which to me is a must for a true egg sandwich.  It was served with home fries, which were sauteed with large slices of peppers and onions.  I'm not the biggest breakfast potatoes fan, but these were great and I appreciated that they didn't clearly just scoop some food from a huge pile of pre-cooked home fries.

The pancakes were great and fluffy.  My one gripe was their use of smuckers pre-packaged syrup.  I realize that if they put syrup in a container, it probably wouldn't be real maple syrup, but I sort of wish I didn't know that they were giving me sub-par syrup.

The server was friendly and very attentive.  The coffee refills were constant, and the coffee was actually good (so many diners fail at coffee).  Bonus points for the server agreeing not to judge my decision to get two breakfasts.

All around, I loved this place and hope to go back soon.  Long live the Jersey diners!
Refine this for me please:
Thank you for a lovely morning! I was in New Jersey early and decided to stop in for a classic diner breakfast. Faced with the eternal sweet-versus-savory dilemma, I indulged in both: a Taylor ham, egg, and cheese sandwich and a short stack of blueberry pancakes. Leftovers are never a bad thing.

The sandwich was fantastic. Initially nervous when they were out of Kaiser rolls, I opted for a hamburger bun—an excellent decision. This was no average bun; it was fresh and substantial. They layered the cheese generously, a must for a proper egg sandwich, and served it with home fries sautéed with large slices of peppers and onions. I’m not usually a breakfast potato fan, but these were clearly cooked to order, not scooped from a pre-made pile.

The pancakes were wonderfully fluffy. My only minor complaint was the Smuckers packaged syrup. I know diner syrup rarely is real maple, but part of me wishes I hadn’t seen the packet—ignorance would have been bliss.

Service was outstanding. The server was friendly and attentive, with constant coffee refills of a brew that was actually good—a rarity in many diners. Bonus points for her agreeing not to judge my double breakfast order.

All around, I loved this place and hope to return soon. Long live the Jersey diners!

input:
The new Han Dynasty took over the spot where the old Mid-Atlantic restaurant (with the unchanging menu) was. I like the Han Dynasty here a lot more than the one in Olde City even if I give both 4*. Maybe I'm biased, because I love the service here. They've always been very nice, and came over to check in with me and just make some small conversation when they heard I had a peanut allergy (even though they had no peanuts in any of the dishes I ordered; I think it was Han's sister?). I've been to this Han Dynasty more times in a month than the number of times I've been to the other.

Note though, that the different branches have different specialties. I heard the dan dan mian in Olde City is the best, but the one in UC isn't so good (I wouldn't know since it has peanuts). Overall, I think it;s okay food wise, still not spicy enough as with the other branch. But I like the layout and atmosphere a lot more.

Next, if you go during lunch, you can ask for lunch portions, that are smaller than the dinner portions, and half the menu price! So it's a great lunch place too, alone, or in a group of 2 or 3.
Refine this for me please:
The new Han Dynasty occupies the former Mid-Atlantic restaurant space, which was known for its static menu. While I rate both this location and the Olde City branch four stars, I have a clear preference for this one. My bias likely stems from the exceptional service; the staff are consistently gracious. On learning of my peanut allergy, they made a point to check in and engage in friendly conversation, even though my chosen dishes contained no peanuts (I believe it was Han’s sister who visited my table). I’ve visited this University City location more times in a single month than I’ve ever visited the other.

It’s important to note that each branch has its own specialties. I’ve heard the dan dan mian is best in Olde City, while the UC version is reportedly inferior—I wouldn’t know, as it contains peanuts. Overall, I find the food here good, though still not as spicy as the Olde City offerings. However, I greatly prefer this location’s layout and atmosphere.

A major perk is the lunch service. By requesting lunch portions, you receive a smaller plate for half the menu price, making it an excellent spot for a midday meal, whether you’re dining alone or with a couple of friends.

Carisma Restaurante remains our favorite dining destination. The consistently excellent food and attentive service, led by the friendly owner Jose who visits every table, ensure a wonderful experience. Our recent meal featured two paellas, salmon, and a filet mignon—all made to order, perfectly cooked, and served hot.

input: This is a small hole in the wall in the African section of Woodland Avenue.  Though it might not look like much, there is some good food coming out of its kitchen representing Senegal and West Africa.  I enjoyed the national dish of Senegal - Thiboudienne - although note that here they do a version without the usual tomato sauce.  I also took home a Jollof Rice which is often called the mother dish of Jambalaya.  There are a few hightop tables inside for dining or you can order the food to-go.  Either way, service is friendly.
Refine this for me please:
Tucked along Woodland Avenue’s African strip, this modest spot delivers authentic Senegalese and West African flavors. I tried Thiboudienne, Senegal’s national dish, served here in a unique tomato-free version. Their Jollof Rice—often considered the precursor to Jambalaya—was also excellent. Inside, a few hightop tables offer casual dining, but takeout is a popular option. Whichever you choose, expect genuinely friendly service from this unassuming kitchen.

Refine this for me please: I tried this falafel wrap again today, having remembered it as decent a few years ago. Sadly, it was a major letdown. The only saving grace was the fresh diced cucumber and tomato, but they were buried under that disappointing, flavorless sauce that shouldn’t bear the tzatziki name.

input: Husband and I made a mistake and came here on a Lenten Friday. The wait was forever. But since we were already there, might as well suck it up and see what's it all about. We ordered the blackened alligator and oysters for appetizers, the alligator came out within 15 minutes, and it was alright. A bit too greasy. Then another 15 minutes later, our raw oysters came out, I wanted mine char grilled but the waitress didn't mention they don't have char grilled oysters and still took my order, so I thought I was waiting for mine to be cooked the entire time. When she brought out the two half-dozen raw oyster trays, that's when she told me they only have raw oysters there. SMH. I have sensitive stomach so I only had 3 then gave the rest to my husband. Regardless, the oysters were really fresh. We waited for at least another 20 minutes later for our entrees to come out. At this point, I was really hungry and had hoped we were at home eating ramen noodles instead. My husband had the roast beef po-boy, and I had the tuna and shrimp kabob. My husband told me his roast beef was really salty and while ironically, my kabob was very bland. The kabob came with exactly 3 pieces of cubed tuna, 2 medium size shrimp with plenty of bell peppers and onions in between, and baby shrimp creole with rice. For the ok price, I shouldn't complain too much about this place. Didn't try their seafood boil, but it looked like that would have been a better choice.
Refine this for me please:
My husband and I made the mistake of visiting on a Lenten Friday. The wait was interminable, but since we were already there, we decided to stick it out.

We started with the blackened alligator and oysters. The alligator arrived in about fifteen minutes; it was alright, though a bit too greasy. Another fifteen minutes later, our raw oysters were delivered. I had actually wanted mine char-grilled, but the waitress never mentioned it wasn’t an option and took my order anyway. I spent the whole wait thinking mine were being cooked. She only explained they only served raw oysters when she brought out the two half-dozen trays. Given my sensitive stomach, I only ate three and gave the rest to my husband. To their credit, the oysters were very fresh.

We then waited at least another twenty minutes for our entrees. By then, I was so hungry I wished we were just home eating ramen. My husband had the roast beef po’boy, which he found excessively salty. Ironically, my tuna and shrimp kabob was quite bland. It contained just three cubes of tuna, two medium shrimp, and a lot of bell peppers and onions, served with a side of baby shrimp creole and rice.

For the reasonable price, I can’t complain too much. We didn’t try their seafood boil, but based on what we saw around us, that might have been the better choice.

input:
im going to have to give this place one star for its horrible customer service:

i called in to ask about the 50% off for tulane students they were advertising, the woman assured me if i came with an id it would be half off and made an appointment for me, only once i got there did they tell me it's only on certain days, "it says it right on the sign," i was perturbed by the inconvenience and said so you're not going to honor it even though you just made an appointment with me and told me it would be 50% off, they said no flat out at first even though the error was blatantly on their side, after my nagging, she eventually called john jay himself and he told the woman that he would not honor what i was told even though i had been inconvenienced by someone in HIS staff because it might cause a 'domino effect,' i said how will there be a domino effect unless you continue to give people incorrect information, there will be no other 'dominoes' as long as you remember what day it is from now on... they began to treat me somewhat patronizingly as i explained that usually businesses make concessions when they are the one at fault, that the customer is supposed to always be right, yadda yadda yadda, i left pretty upset and with ~45 minutes of my life having been wasted - empty handed but for a lame excuse from someone who owns at least 3 businesses over 10 dollars...

i have not received a haircut from them so if you're one of those people who ONLY cares about the product and you think you'll get a good cut go right on ahead, but if you're like me (principled) and you don't like handing profits to people who care nothing about their customers this is a good place to skip next time you need a cut
Refine this for me please:
I am giving this establishment a one-star review due to its abysmal customer service.

I called to inquire about the advertised 50% discount for Tulane students. The woman on the phone assured me the discount would apply if I presented my ID and proceeded to book an appointment for me. However, upon my arrival, I was informed the promotion was only valid on specific days, with the employee dismissively noting, "It says it right on the sign."

I was understandably upset by this inconvenience and pointed out that they had just confirmed the discount while making my appointment. Initially, they flatly refused to honor it, despite the error being entirely theirs. After I persisted, the employee called the owner, John Jay. He instructed her not to honor what I was promised, citing concern over a potential "domino effect."

I countered that a domino effect would only occur if they continued to give customers incorrect information. If they simply communicated the policy accurately going forward, there would be no further issues. As I explained that businesses typically make concessions when they are at fault—that the customer should be right—their demeanor became patronizing.

I left feeling deeply frustrated, having wasted 45 minutes and receiving nothing but a feeble excuse from an owner of multiple businesses, all over $10.

I did not get a haircut here, so I cannot comment on the quality of the service itself. If you care only about the end result and believe you’ll get a good cut, you may proceed. But if you are principled, like me, and prefer not to patronize businesses that show such disregard for their customers, this is a place you should skip.

input: Awesome food, great place to split a bunch of delicious spicy, ultra flavorful dishes with a large group. It's the Chinese restaurant a lot of people know about for good reason - I haven't had a single bad dish here, and it's always a crowd-pleaser.

input:
My friend and I visited Tampa for a concert, and about ten minutes away from the Atlanta airport he realized that he had purchased tickets for the wrong day. We had already made hotel reservations and bought the concert tickets, so he just had to pay same-day price for airfare: all in all about $800 more. "It was totally worth it," he later told me, "Because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life."

All because we randomly picked the Bricks of Ybor from Yelp. I can't vouch for the peanut butter or meatless menu, but the meat sandwiches that we bought were absolutely phenomenal. I had the pulled pork, which was flavored with ponzu and served on Hawaiian sweet bread. It was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. We spent a few hours hanging out and drinking, during which time Brian, the owner, came out and talked to us, comped us a drink, let us try new appetizers he was developing (all for free) and generally made us feel really welcome. 

I kept my eyes open to the kind of crowd that came in and out of the restaurant. It seemed to draw everything from hipsters to geriatrics and strait-laced families with young kids. I think it speaks to both the diversity of the menu and the pleasant environment. We went back for drinks before and after the concert. It got very crowded but we still received excellent food, drinks and service. I give this restaurant my strongest recommendation, and it's the first place I'm going when I next visit Tampa.
Refine this for me please:
My friend and I flew to Tampa for a concert. About ten minutes from the Atlanta airport, he realized he’d bought our tickets for the wrong day. With the hotel and concert already booked, he had to swallow the same-day airfare—adding about $800 to the trip. Later, he insisted, “It was totally worth it, because I got to have the best sandwich of my entire life.”

That sandwich came from a random Yelp pick: Bricks of Ybor. I can’t speak to their peanut butter or meatless options, but the meat sandwiches we tried were phenomenal. I had pulled pork flavored with ponzu, served on Hawaiian sweet bread—one of the best meals I’ve had in years. We lingered for hours, and the owner, Brian, came out to chat, comped us a drink, and let us sample new appetizers he was developing, all free of charge. He made us feel genuinely welcome.

I noticed the crowd, too—a mix of hipsters, older regulars, and families with young kids. That diversity speaks to both the varied menu and the pleasant, inviting atmosphere. We returned for drinks before and after the concert. Though the place grew packed, the food, service, and quality never dipped. I give Bricks of Ybor my strongest recommendation. It will be my first stop the next time I’m in Tampa.

We were seated after requested 3 times that the hostess speak a little louder because we couldn't even hear her with the background music. Two other wait staff seemed to be sharing our table, but no idea who was responsible for our table.  We got our drinks and ordered, but food took forever considering there was not more than 15-20 filled tables in the entire restaurant. Only after we received our food did we understand they had already ordered and still did not have their food!  I doubt I will return to this restaurant in the future.

On a mid-afternoon visit with my sister-in-law in August 2015, our experience was disappointing from the start. We had to ask the hostess three times to speak louder over the intrusive background music just to be seated. Our booth faced a television stuck on a looping Larry King vitamin commercial, which was an immediate annoyance.

Service was chaotic. Our waitress introduced herself and a trainee, then vanished. Two other servers intermittently attended our table, creating confusion over who was responsible. While the restaurant was only half-full, our food took excessively long to arrive. The blue cheese burger was decent but overwhelmed by an excessive amount of cheese. The fries and onion sticks, however, were quite good.

Throughout the meal, no one checked on our satisfaction or needs. We had to ask twice and wait for a simple takeout box. The poor service was further highlighted by a family seated nearby when we arrived; we only realized as we ate that they had ordered before us and were still waiting for their meals. Due to this combination of noisy atmosphere, inattentive service, and mismanagement, it is unlikely I will return.

input:

I ended up parking three blocks away and broke a sweat walking in the dead of summer to the front entrance.

The meal was decent but overpriced. The guacamole and my Mojito were the highlights. My peach pork medallions were cooked well yet bland, while the corn cakes with Barbacoa were quite good.

input:
This was a tough one!   On the merits of the wine, fairly average... I understand that the winery has more than one lable and other label is their premium wines.  I look forward to when that is available (I went two weeks ago so maybe it already is)     Location..   what's not to like?  On the pier!  A wonderful outdoor patio,  couldn't have a nicer setting to enjoy your tasting....   The staff were super, super nice,  I would give them an A+!  

So why only three stars?  It is because of the wine club!  Very expensive for the quality of the wines and stingy as HELL with the benefits to the members..   Most wine clubs will give you a free tasting every time you come in (after all, we are your best customers... we are the ones who buy your wine time and time again).  Some wineries will give their members a complimentary glass in leau of a tasting (Carr).   Most wineries allow you to bring guests which is how you get new wine club members.   This system works folks!  The way this wine club works is that you are given a very limited number of passes per quarter, five as I recall.   If I come with my wife once a month we wouldn't even be covered... let alone if we bring a guest!   

So go to this winery if you want to enjoy a tasting in one of the most beautiful settings on earth.   But avoid the wine club!  For that you can pretty much go to any of the other wine tasting rooms on the Urban wine trail.
Refine this for me please:
This was a challenging review to write. Based purely on the wine, the experience was fairly average. I understand the winery has another label for its premium offerings, which I look forward to trying—perhaps it’s available now.

The location, however, is exceptional. Situated right on the pier with a wonderful outdoor patio, it would be hard to find a more beautiful setting for a tasting. The staff also deserves top marks; they were incredibly friendly and would earn an A+.

So, why only three stars? The reason is the wine club. It is very expensive for the quality of wine offered and surprisingly stingy with member benefits. Most clubs provide a complimentary tasting for members each visit—after all, we are their best, repeat customers. Some, like Carr Winery, even offer a complimentary glass instead. Crucially, most encourage bringing guests, which is how clubs typically grow. This system works.

Here, however, members receive a very limited number of passes per quarter—five, as I recall. If my wife and I visit once a month, we wouldn’t even be fully covered, let alone if we brought a guest.

My advice? Visit this winery to enjoy a tasting in one of the most beautiful settings imaginable. But avoid the wine club. For that, you can find better value and hospitality at almost any other tasting room on the Urban Wine Trail.

It's very vegetarian friendly!  The soft tofu is stewed and put into the dol sot pots which each and every stew feels like it's custom made for you. 

You can select from beef, seafood or mixed meats (seafood & beef), mushroom, and just plain.  They can adjust the spice as needed too.  I always get the extra hot with the hot temperature, can't beat it.  The rice also comes in a dol-sot which is great if you leave it in for a while, it burns the rice into a nice crispy shell.  DROOL.

Just thinking about this place makes my mouth salivate!  

If you're not into tofu, they also offer korean bbq meats (cooked in the back), with other soup/stew items.

Love this place!!!

The finest soon-dubu in the city! Tucked away, the moment you enter feels like stepping into a warm and inviting Korean home.

It’s wonderfully vegetarian-friendly. The soft tofu is stewed and served in individual *dol sot* pots, making each bowl feel custom-made.

You can choose from beef, seafood, mixed (seafood and beef), mushroom, or plain. They’ll gladly adjust the spice level—I always order extra hot, which is unbeatable. The rice also comes in a stone pot; letting it sit forms a deliciously crispy shell. Just thinking about it makes my mouth water.

If tofu isn’t for you, they also offer Korean BBQ meats (cooked in the back) and other soup or stew options.

An absolute favorite!
