input:
--------DINNER REVIEW----------

I rarely write reviews, but this honestly was one of the worst group dining experiences I've ever had. It was objectively a horrible experience, even without comparing it to the hype it receives, and ruined what was supposed to be a nice birthday dinner celebration. 

We had a group of 8 that had a reservation made well in advance. Short wait, but not too bad. Keep in mind, it seemed like a normal Friday night, but weren't super busy or at-capacity.

It was a birthday dinner, so I told the hostesses that it was her birthday, and asked if they could bring out something for her at the end of the meal, which was acknowledged. Pretty standard stuff, whether at a Applebee's or the French Laundry. We were sat at a booth right next to the Maitre D' stand, and next to all the wait staff's home base, so pretty much no excuse for not getting any attention. 

After getting us waters, it took them a LONG time to even come by and acknowledge us. After ordering wine, it took them another good 15-20 minutes to even bring us our wine, and no one even checked in on us! (hint: if you're running a restaurant, wine is your profit center and doesn't take any work other than taking a bottle off a shelf and opening it. bring it out ASAP...). 

After ordering food, it was more of the same...a long wait for food to start coming out and no one checking in on us AT ALL. We drank the bottles we ordered and had to get up and flag someone down to get another wine order. A couple of us even got up during the meal to remind them to bring out something for birthday girl at the end of the meal. 

Once our meal was done and taken away, we were given dessert menus and the server disappeared for 10-15 minutes... AGAIN. After coming back, he asked what dessert we wanted, so we ordered some coffees... and waited... and waited. Eventually we got up and asked him what was going on and if they were going to bring anything out like we asked multiple times. 

They finally brought out a couple of cookies with a candle...

In summary, the food was pretty hit or miss, pretty mediocre for this price point. Whipped feta, like other reviews have said, was amazing, and the Braised Lamb was really good. But the Sirloin was chewy and bland and the Grilled Caesar tasted like a soggy, luke-warm, wilted mess (two orders were left untouched by a group of 8). Atmosphere was nice and trendy. But the service, which is a huge reason to spend your hard-earned $ at a restaurant, was absolutely horrendous. 

I really love going to cool, popular restaurants and having a great time, and I hate writing such a negative review, but I had to share my experience, especially for a restaurant that is getting an awful lot of (undeserved) hype.
Refine this for me please:
--------DINNER REVIEW----------

I seldom write reviews, but this was, without exaggeration, one of the most disappointing group dining experiences I can recall. The evening was objectively poor, independent of the considerable hype surrounding the restaurant, and it thoroughly undermined a planned birthday celebration.

Our party of eight had a reservation made well in advance. We were seated after a brief, reasonable wait on what appeared to be a typical Friday night—the restaurant was not at capacity.

At the outset, I informed the hostesses it was a birthday dinner and requested a small acknowledgment for the guest of honor at the meal’s conclusion—a standard courtesy anywhere from casual chains to fine dining. We were placed at a booth adjacent to the Maître D' station and the main service aisle, essentially at the staff's epicenter. This location made the subsequent neglect inexcusable.

After delivering water, the staff took an exceptionally long time to acknowledge us. Once we ordered wine, another 15-20 minutes passed before the bottles arrived, with no check-in in between. (A basic operational note: wine is a key profit driver requiring minimal preparation; it should be prioritized.) The pattern persisted after ordering food. Courses arrived slowly, and we were completely ignored throughout. We finished our wine and had to physically flag someone down to order more. Multiple reminders about the birthday acknowledgment were necessary, delivered by guests leaving the table to find staff.

When the meal concluded and plates were cleared, we were given dessert menus. Our server then vanished for another 10-15 minutes. Upon his return, we ordered coffee and desserts, only to be met with another prolonged wait. Finally, we rose to inquire about both the order and the forgotten birthday gesture. The acknowledgment, when it eventually came, was a couple of cookies with a candle.

Regarding the food, it was inconsistent and mediocre for the price point. As other reviews note, the whipped feta was excellent, and the braised lamb was very good. However, the sirloin was chewy and bland, and the grilled Caesar salad arrived as a soggy, lukewarm, wilted mess—two full orders remained untouched by our group of eight. The atmosphere itself is stylish and trendy.

Yet service is a fundamental reason to spend hard-earned money at a restaurant, and here it was utterly horrendous. I take no pleasure in writing such a negative assessment, but given the substantial (and, in my experience, undeserved) acclaim this place receives, I felt compelled to share this candid account. A special occasion was spoiled by inattentive, disorganized service that no level of hype can justify.

input:
Second stop for Center City Restaurant Week:  R2L, dinner for $35 each. 

On the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place is a very fancy-cool restaurant/lounge where you can get a bird's eye view of the city! Group of us went to dinner here together after a day of meetings. Didn't get one of the tables facing the windows, but still had great views of the sunset and city by night. Again, multiple choices for the three courses, but I chose to start with the crisp peas/ham/garlic risotto [balls]. Main course was the Butcher's Filet (braised short rib + Steuben bean chili, potato/farm veg slaw and basil), which was quite heavy since there was also meat in the chili as well. The dazzling dessert to finish it off was the milk chocolate + hazelnut pudding served with salted caramel and coffee to melt the chocolate, and candied almonds on the side. A bottle of wine for the table as well. Food was great, waiter was awesome (making sure to warn me that the risotto came in ball form rather than a bowl, for instance), very classy experience.
Refine this for me please:
Our second stop for Center City Restaurant Week was R2L, where we enjoyed a three-course dinner for $35 each. Perched on the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place, this sophisticated restaurant and lounge offers a breathtaking bird’s-eye view of the city. Our group dined there together after a day of meetings. Although we didn’t secure a window table, we still enjoyed spectacular views of the sunset and the glittering city at night.

The menu provided multiple choices for each course. I began with crisp pea, ham, and garlic risotto balls. For the main, I had the Butcher’s Filet—a braised short rib served with Steuben bean chili, potato and farm vegetable slaw, and basil. It was quite hearty, especially with the additional meat in the chili. The meal culminated with a dazzling dessert: milk chocolate and hazelnut pudding accompanied by salted caramel, coffee to melt the chocolate, and candied almonds on the side. We also shared a bottle of wine.

The food was excellent, and our waiter was attentive—even thoughtfully warning me that the risotto came as balls, not in a bowl. It was a truly classy experience.

input:
I moved from Chicago to Philadelphia over a year ago.  Everybody here raves about the restaurants, but I have yet to find many that deserve five stars, or even four.  This is the best restaurant I have eaten in in Philadelphia.  

Tahini and bread  arrived at the table, and I thought, hum, plain but I'm hungry.  They must put crack in that Tahini.  I wanted to lap it out of the bowl like an uncouth dog.  The bread is excellent too.

I love a menu with many organic meat choices.  How often can you order an organic beef shishkabob?  It was superb.  The meat done perfectly, the onions nearly caramelized but not quite so they still had some substantive crunch.  The purslane salad tasted like I was eating a plant in the middle of a garden.  It is not often that I dream about a salad but I do dream about this one

My husband had a chicken dish with black eyed peas and green peas and fantastic rice.  I won't begin to describe the flavoring; it is beyond my culinary vocabulary.  We asked what spices they use, and in addition to traditional zatar, they use their own blend of spices.  I don't even need to know what is in it just so long as we can keep coming back and ordering it again and again.

I was so full but ate dessert none the less, which I usually don't do.  But when a diner is this good, I had a feeling the desserts would be too and I just needed to find out.  Pistachio creme brulee.  It could have come out over the top, but no indeed.  It was pure pistachio heaven in s super light yet rich custard.  Heaven. Heaven.

Our service was superb.  The squeezed us into a last minute Friday night reservation with the caveat that we would need to get through our dinner in an hour and 15 minutes in order to accommodate a reservation made prior to us.  Given the time constraints they never made us feel rushed and timed the meal perfectly.  Then my husband left to go to the restroom, the waiter picked up his napkin and refolded it nicely on the table.  Do I care about the napkin placement in the middle of a meal?  Not really, but it is a sign that the waitstaff is incredibly attentive and extremely well trained.  

My eating out plan for Philly might just be to skip eating most everywhere most of the time so I can frequent this expensive, though appropriately priced restaurant.  Kudos to the chef.
Refine this for me please:
After more than a year of living in Philadelphia, having moved here from Chicago, I’ve heard constant praise for the city’s dining scene. Yet, I’ve found few establishments that truly earn a four- or five-star rating in my book. This restaurant is the exception—it is, without question, the best I have experienced in Philadelphia.

The meal began simply with tahini and bread. My initial thought was, “Plain, but I’m hungry.” That changed with the first taste. The tahini was so inexplicably delicious I joked they must lace it with something addictive; I wanted to lick the bowl clean. The accompanying bread was also excellent.

I was immediately drawn to a menu featuring numerous organic meat options—a rarity. I ordered the organic beef shish kebab, and it was superb. The meat was cooked perfectly, and the onions were nearly caramelized yet retained a satisfying, substantive crunch. The purslane salad tasted astonishingly fresh, as if plucked straight from a garden. It is rare for me to dream about a salad, but I have dreamed of this one.

My husband chose a chicken dish served with black-eyed peas, green peas, and fantastic rice. The flavor profile was so complex it defies my culinary vocabulary. When we inquired about the spices, we learned they use traditional za’atar alongside a proprietary house blend. I don’t need to know its secrets—only that we can return to enjoy it again and again.

Despite being full, I felt compelled to try dessert, a departure from my usual habit. My reasoning was simple: a restaurant this exceptional would surely excel here, too. The pistachio crème brûlée confirmed it. It could have been overly rich, but instead, it was a masterpiece—a super light yet decadent custard offering pure pistachio heaven.

The service matched the quality of the food. They accommodated a last-minute Friday night reservation with the caveat that we would need to conclude within an hour and fifteen minutes. Despite this constraint, we never felt rushed; each course was timed perfectly. At one point, my husband stepped away, and our waiter discreetly picked up his fallen napkin, refolding it neatly on the table. While napkin placement mid-meal isn’t a personal priority, it signaled an incredibly attentive and well-trained staff.

My new Philadelphia dining strategy may be to forgo meals elsewhere, saving both appetite and budget for this restaurant. It is expensive, yet every dollar feels justified. My highest compliments to the chef.

input:
Uhhhhh.... Not sure how to quantify or qualify my experience here. Let's start with back story: 

My sister was visiting for the weekend, so I wanted to show her a solid night on the town that lasted till the wee hours of the morning. We started on Frenchmen, but for whatever reason it was dead. 
Deciding to adventure Uptown we proceeded on a respectable bar crawl, including Delachaise, Columns, and St. Joes, however, at 3 AM the usual Uptown culprits start to raise their heads. A summary of the following dialogue:

Friends "Let's go to FMs" 
Me: "No, too much broken glass"
Friends: "Let's go to Snake and Jake's"
Me: "Eh...."
Friends: "Brothers 3?"
Me: "I'm afraid I'll hit my head on the ceiling"
Friends: "The Saint!!"
Me: "I suppose I haven't been there before, I'm curious."

After entering the Saint the look on my sisters face was priceless, akin to a deer in headlights look. I kept my countenance, and we ordered a round. Things proceeded as expected ... unwanted dance grinding advances, check! uber drunk guy talking your ear off, check! Big Buck Hunter, CHECK!!! Overall I'm glad I moderately traumatized my sister and sated my curiosity in the same night. 

Helpful hint: They have outdoor seating, surprisingly, which is very good to escape the smoke
Refine this for me please:
My sister was visiting for the weekend, and I wanted to show her a proper, late-night New Orleans experience. We began on Frenchmen Street, but it was unexpectedly quiet. Seeking more energy, we ventured Uptown for a bar crawl, hitting spots like Delachaise, The Columns, and St. Joe’s. By 3 a.m., the familiar debate over where to end the night began.

My friends suggested various dive bars: F&M’s (“too much broken glass”), Snake and Jake’s (“eh…”), and Brother’s Three (“I’ll hit my head on the ceiling”). Then someone said, “The Saint!” I hadn’t been, so curiosity won.

Upon entering, my sister’s deer-in-headlights expression was priceless. I maintained composure, and we ordered drinks. What followed was a quintessential dive bar checklist: unwanted dance floor advances, an overly drunk conversationalist, and a round of Big Buck Hunter. In the end, I was glad to have both moderately traumatized my sister and satisfied my own curiosity in one night.

A helpful tip: They have outdoor seating, which offers a surprisingly good escape from the indoor smoke.

During a recent trip to Nashville, I made a point of visiting Bell Meade. To put it simply, I enjoyed it so much that I will go out of my way to return on every future visit.

Even so, I had a wonderful time. I sampled a few offerings at the tasting bar and, even better, had a fantastic conversation with Max. His knowledge and hospitality are a major reason I’ll be back.

input:
I love trying fresh seafood on piers, wharfs and seaside markets. Most of the time, it is a disappointing experience but this place is not. The food is legitimately fresh and prepared well. The gorgeous view is just a cherry on top of nature's beautiful sundae. I have been here before but ordered the "wrong" thing (cioppino). That wasn't very good when I had it a couple of years ago here. 

We came for a late lunch/early dinner on a Monday. Even at 4pm,  there was a wait! We waited about 25 minutes and got a table outdoor. While it wasn't ideal that we sat right in the sun with no shelter other than our sunscreen and sunglasses, the view was worth it. 

We got the local crab special which was a steamed 3-lb. crab served with a salad and soup for $26. I thought this was quite the steal because the crab was huge, delicious and meaty. The garden salad was fresh as simple as it was. The lobster bisque we got was pretty good. (The other options were Caesar salad and clam chowder). They topped off the crab with a couple of onion rings and cups of cocktail sauce and drawn butter. Yum!

We also got the fried platter of shrimp, oysters, calamari and scallops for $12.95. It came with cole slaw, onion rings, tartar sauce and cocktail sauce. As greasy of a meal as this made, it was one of the better fried platters I've had anywhere. The seafood was just really fresh including the sometimes-feared fried oyster. :)

The ice in our iced teas melted away in the sun. Our waitress was so cool and brought us lots of extra ice and an extra iced tea in case we needed it (we did because it was hot out!). She was just friendly and good at her job - five stars for her!

By the time we left at about 6, there were so many people waiting. Make sure you sign up for a seat on the clipboard right when you get there. The restaurant is the last one at the very end of the pier. Parking on the pier is free for 90 minutes but it looks like a drive that will upset tires. I parked in the large lot south of the pier and walked 15 minutes up and onto the pier. It was free on a Monday late afternoon.
Refine this for me please:
Of all the simple seaside pleasures, few are as enticing—or as routinely disappointing—as ordering fresh seafood right off the pier. Too often, the view outshines the meal. This place, however, is a glorious exception, where the food is legitimately fresh and expertly prepared, making the gorgeous ocean vista merely the cherry on top of nature’s beautiful sundae. A prior visit years ago, when I mistakenly ordered the cioppino, had left me underwhelmed. This recent trip completely redeemed it.

We arrived for a late lunch on a Monday, and even at 4 p.m., there was a wait—a promising sign. After about 25 minutes, we secured an outdoor table. Though we were seated directly in the sun with only sunscreen and sunglasses for shelter, the panoramic view made the glare worthwhile.

Our first choice was the local crab special: a massive, steamed three-pounder served with soup and salad for just $26. It was a remarkable steal. The crab was deliciously meaty, the garden salad was crisp and simple, and the lobster bisque was rich and flavorful. The platter was finished perfectly with onion rings, cocktail sauce, and drawn butter.

We also sampled the fried seafood platter for $12.95, featuring shrimp, oysters, calamari, and scallops, accompanied by coleslaw, onion rings, and sauces. While it was an undeniably greasy feast, it ranked among the best I’ve ever had. Every component was notably fresh—even the sometimes-intimidating fried oyster was tender and sweet.

The sun swiftly melted the ice in our teas, but our waitress was wonderfully attentive, bringing extra ice and a replenished drink without being asked. Her friendly, efficient service deserved five stars all on its own.

By our 6 p.m. departure, the crowd had grown considerably. A helpful tip: sign your name on the clipboard near the entrance immediately upon arrival. The restaurant is the very last one at the pier’s end. While pier parking is free for 90 minutes, the rugged road seems tire-unfriendly. Instead, I used the large free lot south of the pier and enjoyed the 15-minute stroll onto the pier—a small price to pay for a meal that finally lived up to the view.

---

I stayed at the Orange St location from Friday to Monday.

Arrival: I already read plenty of reviews about no signs marking the location therefore, I looked for Starbucks. I parked in a spot in front of the multi business complex. I went inside to find a guard at a desk that said we have been contracted to hand guests their keys and room number and nothing more. He advised me there was a phone that was on the wall that I could make a call to someone if I needed to. He also stated that the very few parking spots in front were free* only on the weekend.

The Room: This wasn't a room, this was an apartment and I absolutely loved it. It was very spacious and had everything I sought* after for that weekend, such as: fully stocked kitchen, a desk, lots of space, king bed, huge table, nice living room, lots of closets. My only complaint is that I could not open any windows for fresh air...they are nailed/screwed shut. There was also a small welcome bag w cookies and water and papers letting you know where all the food delivery locations and numbers.
There wasn't maid service knocking loudly or trying to barge in early in the morning. This place is more of a long term setting and I'm sure the maids come around during the week Monday-Friday if you desire. I was only here for 3 days and I was fine with that. I went shopping at Shoprite and filled my fridge with water and breakfast to cook.

Overall: This place is awesome, I had a huge living room to entertain my guests when they visited, and a nice desk to study my Anatomy notes. I forgot to mention how quiet** this place is. I loved it. I felt as if no one was there except me. Very quiet* which worked for me on Sunday bc I had lots of studying to do and two TV's to watch The Walking Dead on. Lol!  I would most definitely stay here again. Very spacious and updated. Loved it!
Refine this for me please:
I stayed at the Orange Street location from Friday to Monday.

**Arrival:** Having read reviews about the lack of signage, I looked for the nearby Starbucks. I parked in a spot in front of the multi-business complex and went inside. A guard at the desk informed me they were only contracted to hand out keys and room numbers. For any questions, he pointed to a wall phone to call someone. He also noted the few front parking spots were complimentary only on weekends.

**The Room:** This was more an apartment than a room, and I absolutely loved it. It was incredibly spacious and had everything I needed: a fully stocked kitchen, a desk, a king bed, a large dining table, a nice living room, and ample closet space. My sole complaint was that the windows were sealed shut, preventing fresh air. A small welcome bag contained cookies, water, and information with local food delivery details. The absence of daily maid service was a plus—no loud knocks or early disturbances. This is clearly set up for longer stays, with service likely available on weekdays. For my three-day stay, it was perfect. I shopped at Shoprite to stock the fridge with water and breakfast items.

**Overall:** This place is awesome. The huge living room was ideal for entertaining visiting guests, and the desk provided an excellent study space for my anatomy notes. I must emphasize how remarkably quiet the building was; I often felt like the only person there. This peaceful atmosphere was perfect for my intensive Sunday study session, and having two TVs to watch *The Walking Dead* was a great bonus. The unit was very spacious, modern, and updated. I would definitely stay here again. Loved it!

The ordeal began when I made the mistake of purchasing a vehicle beyond my budget on a Friday afternoon. By Sunday, after reviewing my finances, I realized I could not afford it. I called the salesman at 11:30 a.m. to explain my situation. He said he would consult his manager and call me back. By 3:30 p.m., with no callback, I tried him again—no answer. On Monday morning, I arrived as the dealership opened. I asked Stephen, the salesman, for an update. He told me to have a seat while he spoke with management. Over an hour later, I was called into a cubicle and informed my loan had been funded and the title processed. Consequently, they stated my only option was to sell the car back to them as a used vehicle, incurring a significant financial loss.

However, this morning, Bill, the head of finance, advised that the bank had questions about funding. I then received a direct call from the bank confirming the loan had **not** been approved and would not be funded. Despite leaving numerous messages for the dealership, I have received no callback. After consulting an attorney, I called again, requesting a time to return the vehicle and reclaim my trade-in. Still, there has been no response.

This dealership will lie to your face. I urge you to avoid it entirely.

input:
I have been a patron of Desi Village in West Philly for years.  After moving the suburbs, we saw the KOP Desi Village and finally tried it.  We were skeptical having also tried Mood Cafe (owned by the W.Philly folks), and it wasn't as good. But the KOP location is actually very comparable to the West Philly location.  

There is no ambiance or atmosphere here.  The strip mall where it's located is pretty depressing.  Desi Village may be the only active store in it.  And its decor is tired and old.  It is a big space and it appears they do a big lunch buffet but I'm curious if it's ever full.  So don't go for the ambiance.

But the food is good.  We ordered some Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani.  All of it was really good.  Perfectly seasoned, not too oily, and appropriately spicy.  I have a nut allergy and made them aware of that and they did not screw it up (most Indian restaurants do).  So we'll definitely be back.  It would be great if they moved into nicer digs but the food is what is most important.
Refine this for me please:
As a longtime patron of Desi Village in West Philly, I was skeptical of their King of Prussia location, especially after a disappointing experience at their sister restaurant, Mood Cafe. However, the food here is genuinely comparable to the original.

Do not come for the ambiance. The restaurant sits in a nearly vacant, depressing strip mall, and the interior decor is tired and dated. It’s a large space that seems built for a busy lunch buffet, though it’s hard to imagine it ever being full.

Come strictly for the food, which is excellent. Our order of Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani was all perfectly seasoned, not overly oily, and had just the right level of spice. Importantly, they handled my nut allergy with care—a notable reliability many Indian restaurants lack.

We will definitely return. While a nicer setting would be welcome, the quality of the meal is what matters most.

input:
What an AMAZING occurrence that we ended up here after another barbecue place ran out of food!

So yeah, we started out at another spot and they were out of food when we got there. Super bummed and still in the mood for barbecue, we started wandering around Mid City and my trusty Yelp app guided me to this place. We were greeted by the super nice woman working the counter and she explained the whole process.

I decided to get the one-meat plate with "wet" pulled pork, grits and potato salad, I also got a medium mac and cheese, because I can. My boyfriend got the two-meat plate with brisket and pulled chicken with potato salad and fries. The food blew us both away! It was delicious from beginning to end. The pulled pork was perfect and had the perfect amount of sauce without being drenched. I could tell that if I hadn't ordered it wet it still would have been able to stand on it's own. The mac and cheese was incredible, and after the pork, was my favorite part of the meal. The stone ground grits had a different type of flavor (almost smoky) that I enjoyed and the potato salad was served cold and had that nice crunch that I like in potato salad,

We both agreed that the food was excellent, and a good deal to boot, and that we would both make the trip back out to Earhart, just to have more of this delicious food. The owner himself was bringing the food out to folks and he was really friendly and made sure that we were happy with everything. I like when the owners take the time to make sure that everything is okay. The atmosphere is casual and comfortable and the entire process was a breeze. I will definitely return to LA Smokehouse and I'll be adding it to my "BBQ Favorites" list for future reference.
Refine this for me please:
What an incredible stroke of luck that we ended up here after our initial barbecue choice had run out of food!

Our evening began with a disappointment: arriving at another spot only to find them sold out. Still determined for barbecue, we wandered through Mid City until my Yelp app pointed us to LA Smokehouse. We were immediately welcomed by a wonderfully friendly woman at the counter who patiently explained how everything worked.

I opted for the one-meat plate with “wet” pulled pork, choosing stone-ground grits and potato salad as my sides, and couldn’t resist adding a medium mac and cheese. The pulled pork was perfect, sauced just enough without being soggy; I could tell it would have been flavorful even ordered “dry.” The mac and cheese was incredible and ranked as my second favorite after the pork. input:
After today's lunch, Iris has moved to the top of my New Orleans favorites lists--no small feat in a city where restaurants are numerous and culinary competition is fierce. Iris excels in every area: food, drinks, service, atmosphere, location, music and overall graciousness. I made the reservation for 10-15 people, not knowing exactly how many in my party would show up. Iris pulled out all the stops to make sure everyone had comfortable seating and even prepared an overflow table for us. At no time did we feel jostled or rushed, which is a common fine dining concern. 

The layout of the restaurant allowed diners to move freely to and from the table and to exchange seats as needed. The music selection was fun and unique, ranging from the Magnetic Fields to Johnny Cash. It was also quiet enough to be enjoyed while allowing conversation to flow unimpeded. Our waiter had excellent timing and anticipated our every need. 

Though they don't have a full drink menu for lunch (I hear they have an amazing mixologist for the dinner hour) they do offer a selection of martinis and wines. One of the guests has accounts with several high-end bars in the Quarter, and the drink list passed his muster. Our table settled for Chardonnays, Perseco and chilled shots of Chartreuse, though I hear they have several types of absinthe as well. 

Our group began with slices of warm, heavenly bread that Iris bakes in house. We continued with an assortment of salads--I had the Hollygrove arugula with warm goat cheese, niçoise olives and balsamic vinaigrette. It was fresh perfection. A few of us opted for the mussels, which I heard were delicious. For my main course, I had a wonderful drum with onions prepared in a tangy soy reduction, which was an elegant complement for the fish. I also heard rave reviews about the gnocci and chicken. 

All the entrees were creatively arranged and selected, and at no point did I feel overwhelmed or that any fuss or pretense had gone into the food. I also appreciated that the portions were European-sized (it always makes me laugh when other Americans list too-small portion size as a complaint even when the food is well-prepared!). Iris prepares a lot of their basic ingredients in-house, and I appreciate that the kitchen makes a point of incorporating gulf fish and produce purchased from local, farmer-friendly markets. 

We settled on the prix fixe menu, which was $20 a person for appetizer, main course and the dessert of the day (the best strawberry sorbet I have had yet). With the added drinks and tip it came out to under $35 a person, which is an excellent price for such a delicious white-linen lunch. No matter the size of my group, I will definitely be returning!
Refine this for me please:

input:
Great atmosphere and decor. Super friendly staff seat you right away. I stopped once for lunch and one time for dinner. They have some lunch specials one of which was Pad Thai. I order with chicken as the protein but they have the typical options for this .  The portion was good for lunch and had good flavor.

For dinner I ordered the chicken satay to start and the Panang Curry with chicken for main course. I was very disappointed in the satay being that you only get two small skewers. The flavor and peanut dipping sauce were very good but they give a few more skewers.  The Panang was good and you get a good size portion of rice.

On a side note, I was disappointed they do not have Pad See Ew. Still some other options on the menu I will return to try.

The staff and manager really know customer service.  Look forward to returning soon!
Refine this for me please:
The atmosphere and decor are excellent, and the super friendly staff seat you promptly. I visited for both lunch and dinner. At lunch, I tried a special—the Pad Thai with chicken—which offered a well-portioned, flavorful meal.

For dinner, I started with chicken satay. While the flavor and peanut sauce were very good, I was disappointed to receive only two small skewers; a few more would be reasonable. My main course, the Panang Curry with chicken, was satisfying and came with a generous portion of rice.

A minor disappointment was the absence of Pad See Ew on the menu, though there are still other dishes I plan to try next time.

Overall, the staff and manager excel in customer service. I look forward to returning soon.

input:
We see Dr. Gloudemans, and she's a wonderful doctor. Friendly, upbeat, up on the most recent research, and pro-vaxx (hooray!!). She's proactive about problems after making sure things are worth worrying about-- "let's keep an eye on this, and if there's still a problem in a month or two, come back in and we'll see about a referral to a specialist."

As others have mentioned, we've had a few billing hiccups. We received a bill saying we were past due on 3 appointments' fees, despite paying all copays in the office. Luckily it was all straightened out after a phone call, but it's been frustrating on that front.
Refine this for me please:
Dr. Gloudemans is a wonderful physician. She is friendly, stays current with research, and is strongly pro-vaccination. Her approach is proactive yet measured; she carefully assesses issues and will often suggest monitoring something before pursuing a specialist referral, advising a follow-up if a concern persists.

Our only frustration has been with billing. On one occasion, we received a past-due notice for three appointments despite having paid all copays at the office. A phone call resolved the error, but such administrative hiccups have been a recurring annoyance.

input: I work at the Frist and I don't eat at the cafe much, since I like to leave the building and go home for lunch. Beware of Senior Mondays (every 3rd Monday of the month) and weekends at lunchtime- it's usually busiest at 1130-noon.

input:
I really like Prep & Pastry - we have been twice in the last two months on a Sunday.  The best trick I learned is to put your name on the waitlist BEFORE YOU ARRIVE.  As long as you are within 5 miles of the restaurant, you can be added.  It is a great service.

I have tried a number of things for brunch and all have been excellent - even their sweets. I think my favorite is the breakfast sandwich.  I am not a big drinker, so I usually order the ice team and it really is better than almost anything else I have tried. 

Staff is really, really nice.  I highly recommend a visit if you are in town.

Prep & Pastry has become a favorite—we’ve visited twice in the last two months for Sunday brunch. My top tip is to join the waitlist remotely; you can add your name from within a five-mile radius, which is a fantastic service.

Every brunch dish I’ve tried has been excellent, including their pastries. The breakfast sandwich is my personal favorite. Since I’m not a big drinker, I usually order the iced tea, which is notably better than most.

The staff is exceptionally friendly. I highly recommend stopping by if you’re in the area.

input:
Another great annual festival Edmonton has to offer.

The Fringe is over two weekends and the joining week full of performances. There's a variety of venues and plays to watch, street performers and musicians. There's a schedule online to find show times, buy tickets and learn more about the artists. 

Half of 104th closes down to add space for a variety of food vendors and artisan vendors (art, jewelry, clothing, etc.).

Good tip: there's a gourmet mini donut truck off behind the farmers market a bit tucked away. Amazing!

It's nice to take an hour or two before or after a show to walk around and casually stumble on other street performances. Or even go without seeing a play just to snack and shop at the vendors.

The location is absolutely fabulous.
Refine this for me please:
Edmonton’s Fringe Festival is a vibrant annual event spanning two weekends and the week in between. The schedule is packed with diverse performances across multiple venues, featuring everything from plays to street musicians. For show times, tickets, and artist details, the online schedule is essential.

A section of 104th Street closes to accommodate an array of food and artisan vendors, offering art, jewelry, clothing, and more. A pro tip: seek out the gourmet mini-donut truck tucked behind the farmers’ market—it’s exceptional.

The location itself is fabulous. Whether you attend a show or not, it’s wonderful to spend an hour or two simply wandering, discovering impromptu street performances, sampling treats, and browsing the stalls.

input:

I was eagerly anticipating today’s lunch, only to be disappointed by a clear decline in service. Our server was unsmiling, declined to offer a recommendation, and didn’t provide a complimentary tea to go—a courtesy that was once standard from the formerly friendly staff.

input:

input:
A great spot to take out-of-town guests. I take all my Chicago friends here and they fall in love. The burgers are incredible and the boozy shakes are like no other. The first time I had horchata shake I honestly had dreams about it for like a week. It's also super centrally located, a quick walk from Wash Ave and other downtown attractions. Great vibe, although I always prefer to get a table upstairs than sit at the community tables on the ground floor.

The burger selection is really, really great. You can pretty much get whatever your heart desires. I've had mac n cheese patties on my burger, you can get a bison burger, turkey burger, literally anything. I have tried a ton and have never been let down by the flavor combinations. The waiters are always super honest, in a good way. If you ask them what's better, X or Y, they're not going to jerk you around and say they're equally good. They'll give you their honest opinion. LOVE that. 

Another unique aspect about Bailey's Range is that they have a burger showdown (can't remember their technical term for it) where last week's featured burger goes up against a new burger recipe. It's a cool call-out that you don't see at a lot of other restaurants. 

The only reason I gave it a 4/5 star instead of 5/5 is because I've had a couple of instances (out of MANY visits, so it's really not alarming or anything) where I requested my burger medium or medium-rare and it turned out a little well done. I still ate it, but it wasn't really what I expected.
Refine this for me please:
Bailey’s Range is my go-to spot for entertaining out-of-town guests, especially friends visiting from Chicago, and they consistently fall in love with it. The burgers are incredible, and the boozy shakes are truly unique—my first horchata shake was so memorable I dreamed about it for a week. Its central location is a major plus, just a short walk from Washington Avenue and other downtown attractions. The vibe is always great, though I personally prefer snagging a table upstairs over the communal seating on the ground floor.

The burger selection is outstanding in its variety and creativity. Whether you’re craving a classic beef patty, one topped with mac and cheese, or alternatives like bison or turkey, they have it all. I’ve tried numerous combinations and have never been disappointed by the flavors. The staff adds to the experience by being genuinely honest; if you ask them to choose between two items, they’ll give a straightforward, helpful opinion rather than a vague non-answer.

A fun and unique feature is their weekly burger showdown, where the previous week’s featured burger competes against a new recipe—a creative touch you don’t see everywhere.

My only minor critique, and the reason for a 4-star instead of a 5-star rating, involves occasional inconsistencies in cooking temperature. On a few visits out of many, I’ve requested medium or medium-rare and received a burger that was closer to well-done. It wasn’t enough to ruin the meal, but it did stray from my expectation. Overall, it remains a fantastic and highly recommended spot.
